Summary



   Rocket is captured by a Ravager crew hoping to get rich off the excessively large bounty on
   his head. Throwing a wrench in everyone’s plans is the Terran girl they hired to do some
   freelance assessing on a recent haul of goods they’ve seized from a Xandaran luxury liner.
   Oops.

   or

   girl falls first; raccoon falls harder.

   slight AU starting pre-GOTG volume 1 (but will hit most of the same major plot points).
   slooowww burn + eventual smut. kinda enemies-to-lovers? (but only one of these idiots
   thinks they're enemies). elements of hurt/comfort because rocket is the saddest-angriest boy.
   rating will go up and tags will be added to as needed.

Chapter Summary



      in which our reluctant heroes meet atop a crate of Sovereign porn in the bowels of a

Chapter Notes

   The Eclector is dark and, despite the raucous laughter and fighting of the crew, every footfall
   on the gridded catwalks seems to echo. It smells like rust and oil and old metal, and
   sometimes sweat, and there’s generally very little that is pleasant about it.



   But Kraglin Obfonteri had sent word that the Yondu clan had recently overtaken a Xandaran
   luxury liner. Among its treasures, there had been a pretty vast art collection, and Jolie is a
   reliable assessor and - for some of the more common mediums, as well as a few blindingly
   unique ones - a restorer. It’s not the first time she’s contracted her services out to a Ravager
   crew. Hell, it’s not even the first time she’s worked with the Yondu Clan. She crosses paths
   with them at least once every fifteen cycles or so.



   So here she is, following some hulking brute named Taserface and dodging when pirates on
   the catwalk above decide to spit over the side.



   What a way to spend my morning, she thinks. There better be something worthwhile in this
   pile of junk.

   holds and corridors, trying to make very awkward conversation and occasionally leering at

   keeps a polite smile on her lips and a dead look in her eyes. She’d been hoping today’s escort
   would be the aforementioned Kraglin, or maybe fellow-Terran Peter Quill. Pete’s been family
   since Jolie met him - almost seven years ago - even if they don’t usually see each other more
   than once every few cycles at most. He’s a handful of years older than her, but his relative
optimism still makes her feel like he’s a sweet, annoying little brother. Frankly, it pulls some
heartstrings, because Jolie has baggage where younger siblings are concerned.



Kraglin, on the other hand, is a remarkably endearing moron, and Jolie kind of adores him,
the same way she adores particularly stupid cats.



Unfortunately, Jolie gathers that Pete has apparently disappeared in his M-Ship without a
word - much to the irritation of the rest of the Yondu clan - and Obfonteri is offsite on orders
from the captain, engaging in some kind of criminal activity or another. So here she is, stuck
with a guy who could’ve picked any name in the galaxy and settled on Taserface.



Each chamber the pirate guides her through is packed with stolen goods, and she keeps her
eyes open in case there’s some incredible artistic masterpiece that has somehow escaped the
haul he’s currently taking her to examine. No luck so far, and Taserface is pulling ahead of
her, trying to impress her by droning on about some recent brawl he’s been in. She zones out
of the conversation, only smiling placidly and nodding vacantly when he glances back at her.

More goods are stacked all around, a disorganized horde of stolen treasures: casks of
silverwine from Vanaheim, crates of shimmering pearls from Morag, pleasure-bots from
Contraxia. At the far end, she sees what looks like the corner of a cage.



Her eyes narrow, and her head tilts.



That’s unusual.



Normally, bounties are housed in the caged cells lining the main corridors just off the belly of
the ship - not hidden, and not mixed in with the loot. As they draw closer, Jolie can just make
out a shadow shifting inside - something the size of a kid.



Her blood runs cold.
She’d heard Yondu and his crew had already been exiled from the loose coalition of Ravager

throat before he jettisons her later.



She hums a little - just a random, thoughtful sort of sound, like the powering up of a
computer processor or Nova machine gun - and slides out of the pilot’s seat. She wiggles past
his cage and walks off the bridge, in the direction of the kitchenette he'd glimpsed when
Taserface and Phaedor had brought him in. It takes just a little longer than he might have
expected, but then she’s back, two plates in hand.



His mouth waters.



The first plate is piled high with rehydrated eggs, fluffy and yellow. Some kind of cold,
smoked fish, and a few strips of grilled orloni that she must have warmed up on a hotplate.
The other is a rehydrator plate - which he’s pretty sure isn’t normally used for eating off - but
it’s full of fruit: transparent, jewel-like berries he knows from a brief stop on Indigarr, some
kind of blushing green stonefruit, and wedges of Xandaran frostmelon. Based on the plate,
he’s guessing it’s all rehydrated rather than fresh - but each piece is practically glowing with
sugary juice.
He swears, if she gives him pellets after taunting him like this…



She sits down on the floor, cross-legged and just a little off-center, and sets both plates next
to the cage, where he can reach them if he wants. She’s watching him, one side of her mouth
screwed up in a little grimace.



“I’m pretty sure you’re a lot smarter than you’re telling me,” she says after a minute.



That takes him back a little. For a split-second, he entertains the idea of abruptly pressing one
paw to his chest, gasping dramatically, and spitting, Who, me? back at her with a probably-
reckless amount of disdain.



“Do you want me to take you somewhere?” she asks. “Do you have a home? Is there
somewhere you want to go? Because we can just go. Whenever and wherever you want.”



He has no idea what to make of that.



Her frown deepens, and her brow furrows, and then she’s reaching out toward the cage. For a
moment, he’s shocked to see that she’s clutching the metal key-plate that’ll open the door to
this rustbucket. The plate hovers over the scanner and Rocket flickers somewhere between
baffled and gleeful, because this will be so much easier if she just expects him to be out and
about -



“Promise not to bite my face off,” she mutters under her breath, and clicks the plate against
the reader without waiting for any kind of reaction.



The door clinks softly. There’s a little burst of air from the release of the lock.



Then it swings open an inch, loose on the hinges.
++++



Before they’d even undocked from the Eclector, Jolie had already decided that she is not
keeping this guy in this fucking cage. Even if he isn’t as smart as she suspects, it’s no way for
anything to have to live. When she sits down on the floor with the dishes full of protein and
fruit, she situates herself and the food to one side of the door, so that she can open his cage
without anything or anyone being in his way.



If he wants to stay inside and eat through the bars, there’s nothing stopping him.



If he wants to come out and shred her jugular, well, there’s nothing stopping that either.



The raccoon watches the door swing open, then looks over at her with shrewd, gleaming
eyes. She nods once.



“Yes, I do realize I’m being extremely stupid.”



He steps out cautiously - first one clawed foot, and then the other. She realizes that he’s
barely had room to stand in there: once he’s out in the open air, he straightens up further,
shoulders rolling back as he stretches his spine.



Her eyes drop to the cruel metal skeleton half-visible beneath the skin and fur of his chest.
The scars look like sloppy incisions carelessly re-sewn, but they also look like burns in some
places: twisted-up, gnarled, angry.



There is no way they don’t hurt.



When she looks back up, he’s eyeing her balefully.



“Sorry,” she murmurs apologetically. “That was fuckin’ rude.” She hesitates. She wants to
say, Fuck whoever did that to you, or maybe, It looks like there might be some infection; can I
get you some ointment? but she’s pretty sure that’ll be the tipping point and she’ll end up a
carcass. Instead, she reaches out one finger and nudges the plate full of eggs and meat. “You
want to eat here or up at the table?”



His eyes flash to hers and then to the countertop-bar just beyond the bridge, and yeah, there’s
no way he doesn’t at least understand what she’s saying.



He’s not moving though - faking ignorance, and doing it badly - and they’re at a stalemate.
Finally, she sighs and picks up both plates. “C’mon,” she says, walking over to the little
dining nook and plopping them in front of one barstool. He hops up so quickly, with so much
agility, she almost doesn’t register the movement. He’s just…on the floor, and then he’s not.



“What do you want to drink?” she asks after a moment. “I’ve got water, Xandaran coffee,
curlflower tea, sourberry juice…” She trails off as he glares at her witheringly. “Sorry? I’ve
got…some cheap Contraxian greenwine?”



He looks slightly mollified and she can’t help it, she’s snorting on a laugh under her breath.



“Cool, so I’ve brought home a sommelier.” She flicks a teasing smile at him as she pulls a
bottle out of the compact-chiller, then tilts her head at him consideringly. “Glass? Or bowl?”



His brow flattens into the most dead-eyed expression she’s ever seen, like he’s had just about
enough of her shit, and he gestures for the bottle. She surrenders it easily, both palms raised
in submission. She can feel her smile going soft.



Oh, he is fucking funny. The amount of disdain and sarcasm he can put into a glance is
fucking relatable, and sure - maybe she’s a bit predisposed to liking him on account of
finding him all alone in a cargo hold, but she can also tell already that he is deeply likable in
his own right, independent from her bullshit.



She pulls out a couple forks and a couple knives, setting them on the counter where he can
reach them if he wants. His eyes flicker toward them, and she can see him lingering on the
blades, but she just rolls her neck and shoulders out and takes one of the forks for herself.
Then she reaches out, stabs a clump of egg off his plate, and pops it into her mouth.
His face snaps up to hers, and he cannot hide the look of sheer shock and outrage on his face.
It’s probably very, very foolish to be teasing a three-foot, angry-eyed lifeform with sharp
nails and teeth who already looks like he wants to murder her, but she absolutely cannot help
herself at this point. She grins and winks at him, turning away and tossing her fork in the
sonic sink.



“Eat up,” she tells him. “Then you’re going to help me figure out where we’re going next. Oh
- and I think the bag they threw on the copilot’s seat has your stuff in it,” she adds.



She ducks back onto the bridge while he eats, pulling up a few different sections of the
galaxy on the screens. If he uses the silverware, she doesn’t know. She’s surprised to hear the
clinking of dishes being tossed in the sink, though, and she wonders how long they’re going
to play this game, where he pretends not to be intelligent and she pretends not to notice he’s
hiding it. When he joins her on the bridge, he’s polishing off the bottle of greenwine and
wiping his mouth with one forearm.



She tsks. “Didn’t even save any booze for me.” She flicks a little sideways smile at him.
“Retribution for the eggs?”



He glowers and reaches for the sack of stuff on the copilot’s chair. He rifles through and she
averts her eyes when he pulls out a jumpsuit. When he comes back into her peripherals, he’s
wearing a creased shirt he must’ve also had stuffed in there. She sees him slide something
shiny and square into one of his pockets, but if there was anything else he’d had before -
firearms or tech - she’s pretty sure they’re long gone now.



He watches her for a minute and she pretends not to notice, letting him take as long as he
wants to assess her. She does, however, slide to one side so he can join her at the screens
when he’s ready. He sidles up beside her warily, slanting her a suspicious glance from the
corner of his eye.



Finally, his gaze turns up to the series of maps, and then narrow. She waits as he plants one
paw on the pilot’s seat and launches himself up so he can sort through the screens himself. It
takes a few moments, but then he's tapping a tiny, remote planet that she knows very well
indeed. Its infographic and coordinates expand on the screen at his touch: Conjunction.
“That’s a choice,” she murmurs, glancing down at him and then gazing thoughtfully at the
screen. She taps into an additional layer, and a number of jobs come up in the area - nothing
really lucrative, but enough that she can keep her new copilot in fish and eggs for a while,
and cover any low-grade maintenance that needs doing on the Gemma Lynn. “What are you
trying to do out there, friend?”



She doesn’t expect an answer, so she’s not disappointed. Conjunction is far in terms of
physical distance, but the jump points line up in such a way that it’ll take less time to get
there than it would to travel to many of the more neighboring locations. With that cushion of
timing - and the fact that they need units to keep the ship running - she puts in bids for a
couple shorter jobs on the way and a larger project while she’s there.



“Two and a half days,” she tells him. “We could go quicker but we’ll be tight on fuel and
food without these gigs.” She lets her fingers float over the two mid-way stops she’s bid on.
She knows she’ll get them, because she’s pretty much the best at what she does. And the one
on Conjunction - well, that’s a job already as good as secured, even if it’s not lucrative.



“All right,” she says then, stretching her arms up over her head. Her shoulders and spine pop
and click, and she rolls her neck again. “Want a tour?”



He hits her with that flat, deadpan expression again, and she’s once more lifting her hands in
surrender, trying to hide a grin and failing. “Okay, okay.” She shrugs a shoulder, dropping her
hands. “I’m going to go shower. There are three open bunks - feel free to take your pick of
them. The run of the ship is yours, and we’ll start making our way to Conjunction tomorrow.”
She nudges the cage on the floor with a disdainful boot. “We’ll get rid of that bullshit on the
way.”



She starts to turn, and stops, eyes flicking back to him. “What do you want me to call you?”



He’s still staring at the screens, ignoring her.



Her shoulders melt a little. “Okay,” she says softly, and quirks a quiet, private little half-smile
at the side of his head. One ear swivels toward her. “My name’s Jolie.”
Nothing.



She feels her heart go soft, and her expression with it. “Get some rest at least. And please
don’t murder me in my sleep.”



She turns and pads away out of the cockpit.



++++



What a frickin’ moron.



As soon as she’s left - he listens to her make her way down to the mid level, and the sonic
shower pulls enough energy that he can hear it hum throughout the ship - he uses the screens
to pull up his own resources. Those idiot Ravagers hadn’t touched the units he had squirreled
away and stored digitally, and while he doesn’t have much, he’s betting it’s more than the
broad has right now.



He places a few orders to await him on Conjunction. First, a couple damn shirts and
jumpsuits, woven through with fiber-armor. The way she’d gawked at him when he’d
climbed out of that frickin’ cage -



Another pair of pants, and two protective vests. The frickin’ Ravagers had taken all his
firearms, his bombs, his tech. At least they’d given him back a change of clothes and the
patchwork key-plate from CounterEarth, though.



He would’ve gone back for the key-plate.



He searches to make sure some of his preferred black market firearms dealers are still
running around planetside on Conjunction. He won’t make any purchases without seeing the
goods, but it can be helpful to put some feelers out. He opens the Gemma Lynn’s call scanner
and adds a bit of code, creating a hidden tab that taps into a few different bounty networks, so
he can pick up jobs as needed once he’s armed. He scans for tech dealers next - plenty of
those on Conjunction. He needs a couple tricked-out datapads, some combat goggles, any
new gadgets that might catch his eye, and plenty of scrap to work with.



Anything else Rocket needs or wants, he can just steal.



And then, once he has a basic frickin’ survival stash, it’ll be time to go find Groot. With their
own ship, they won’t have to rely on buying passage or stowing away. Together, they can get
back to bounty hunting, to traveling the sky.



The sonic shower turns off, and once he’s sure the broad is in her bunk, he sets out exploring
his new ship. He learns where every stabby, pointy thing in the kitchenette is. He memorizes
the layout of the common areas and the holds. He finds the mechanical room and utility
closets and her pathetic collection of tools and supplies - need to get new sets of those, too, he
notes - and he sets about dismantling that damn cage so he can use it for parts. It’s too rusted
to be good for much, but it’ll make decent shrapnel for a few bombs.



What are you trying to do out there, friend?



Friend. What makes her think she has the right? There’s only three people in the world
who’ve called him “friend” like it’s his name, and they’re all dead.



It’s better than love though. That comment had made him want to put his teeth through her
throat.



He digs around, looking for things he can break open or tinker with. In the kitchenette, he
finds an old rehydrator and a half-burnt hot plate that she’s clearly replaced, but which work
well enough that she’s kept them for spares. She probably won’t notice their absence in the
morning, so now they’re his. He scrapes up a few other mechanical items that he’s pretty sure
she meant to discard or has forgotten about, as well as some superfluous bolts, bits, and
washers he lifts from various locations on the ship where he knows they’re unnecessary.
Between the broken-down cage and these few scavenged items, he’s pretty sure he can at
least keep himself from being bored until they get planetside.
He heads down to midlevel with an armload of his modest stash, debating between setting up
shop in the mechanical room or whichever bunk he ends up choosing. Probably best if it’s the
latter, he decides, and peers into each open door he finds along the way. Only one is closed,
and he assumes that’s where she’s sleeping.



Sure enough, there are three bunks that are empty. They’re tight, like he’d expect, with only a
few feet to walk in - but there’s a lot crammed into the tiny cubes of space. One has a fairly
large shelf-bed built solidly into the walls, and two have smaller beds that hinge so they can
be pushed up and out of the way when not in use. He doesn’t care much about the size of the
bed, but the bigger one also comes with a surprisingly expansive desk built into an adjoining
wall. Between the desk and the honeycomb of shelves and drawers on the third wall, it ends
up being the bunk he picks. He tucks away some of his stolen goods into the drawers and
slides the dismantled cage bars underneath the desk. A second trip secures the rest of his
scavenged stash, and then he’s standing in the middle of his new den, stretching and twisting
to pop his back and roll out his muscles. He rubs irritably at his neck and one shoulder, where
he can feel the screws and pins and tendons ache.



It’s nice to be outta that frickin’ cage.



He heads to the showers, and notices she’s left out a couple extra hand- towels and some
powdered soap and dry shampoo. He hesitates. Was this a mistake or some kind of
meaningless courtesy? Either way, it doesn’t matter; he takes them, and steps into one stall.
In seconds, his fur is being buffeted by warm, highly-pressurized sound waves, dislodging
the layer of grime that built up during his captivity. He dials up the pressure and heat, until
the stream of compressed sound is massaging his burning, twisted-up muscles and scarred
skin.



He relaxes a little. That feels good. He wishes the Gemma Lynn had water-showers, but those
are pretty rare in space, so he’ll just have to rig up a more expansive water filtration system
and set up a shower pod once the ship is fully in his possession.



He leans his head against the wall while the hum of the shower pulses over him, and turns
that annoying little obstacle over in his head a few times. His mouth twitches consideringly.
He doesn’t care one way or another about bloodshed, but the cleanest thing to do would be to
stun her, bag her, and roll her out of the docking bay on Conjunction.
Well, the cleanest thing to do would be to jettison her, but he’ll wait and see how annoying
she gets before he goes that far. He might not care much about bloodshed, but he doesn’t love
the idea of killing innocent people either. Either way, stunning her will be entertaining.



His mind suddenly flashes to the memory of her, shiny hair like a banner he could grab and
eyes sparkling into crescent moons as she snatched a piece of his food right off his frickin’
plate, and ate it. Then she’d winked, laughing right in his damn face.



“Unbelievable,” he mutters to the shower floor, where one clawed foot taps out his agitation.
The audacity. “Nobody’s got no respect.”



Yeah, stunning her would be entertaining as hell. He bets he can rig something out of the hot
plate wiring that he can use to make it happen. He isn’t trying to babysit the broad, though, so
he’ll wait till they’re actually on Conjunction. If he can make himself wait till they get
planetside, he can just toss her off the ship before he leaves. It’s kinda funny to imagine this
spoiled little princess waking up and trying to fend for herself out there, and he’s satisfied
enough by the fantasy that he can feel his mouth curling into a mean little smile.



“Teach you to laugh at me,” he growls under his breath, letting the hum of the shower
dissolve his words before they echo through the chamber.



If he does it right, she might even be conscious enough to know it’s him, and that has the
potential to be even more enjoyable. He snickers, and turns off the shower, sloughing away
any remaining shampoo residue with the hand towels she’s left behind. Then he uses the
sonic sink and some leftover soap to clean his pants as well as he can. He’ll wear the other
jumpsuit for a couple days, but he’ll definitely need the new pants he’s ordered - he’s been
stuck in these for so long, he’s not sure he’s ever gonna get the rankness out of ‘em.



He’s already snatched a long, serrated knife he doesn’t think will be missed from the
kitchenette, and now he slides it into the hidden loops inside one leg of the jumpsuit. He
suspects she may not have more than a single firearm on board - if that. But his search isn’t
over yet.



Thank fuck we’re headed to Conjunction, he thinks.
He steps out into the corridor. At some point during his shower, the Gemma Lynn had
automatically switched over to the sleep rotation, and the corridor lights have dimmed down
to half-power. Ultimately better for him, he thinks, and heads to the closed door of her bunk.



He sniffs at the entrance, pauses, and twitches his ears forward, straining to hear. All he can
register is steady, even breathing. He taps the panel. If she’s locked it, he’s sure he can break
in pretty easily - but of course she hasn’t. He snorts softly as the door slides open, and the
dim light of the corridor paints a pale rectangle on the floor.



She’s a sloping tangle of limbs under the quilt on the shelf-bed. Her stupid satin hair glows in
the half-light, spilling around her and off the side of the thin mattress in a mass of shiny
ribbons. He can’t see anything of her skin except for one hand, palm-up, fingers curved to the
sky. Her breathing doesn’t hitch at all.



Idiot, he sneers.



Silently, he pads in, eyes everywhere. The door slides shut soundlessly behind him. The walls
are papered with curling, crisping rectangles. He peers at a few and he can tell they’re pencil
sketches and pictures of things - landscapes, portraits, a sweeping nebula in a beautiful and
forever sky - but even with his sharp night-vision, it’s a little dark to pick out details.



The dresser is neatly stacked with more papers, pencils, and various tubes. A series of vices
are clamped to the edge of the desk; sheafs of burlap and softly-crinkling paper, string. A few
glimmering but - he suspects - ultimately worthless chunks of crystal perch in one corner. A
couple powdered-down plasma orbs. He lifts a few of the little metal tubes, one at a time, and
sniffs them: paint, and some kind of rubbery glue.



He can use some of these. He pockets a tiny metal tube of adhesive, and one of Indigarran
pigment, which he happens to know is highly combustible. He unclamps two of the vices
with deft fingers, pocketing them soundlessly.



Slowly, quietly, he slides open the drawers. More of the same: a couple texts which might go
for a decent amount - there’s a Shi’ar scroll that looks like it could be worth something, and a
paper book in some kind of Terran language. Paper books are rare in most of the galaxy and
something of a novelty, but still, there’s nothing particularly exciting here.
He continues to explore the perimeter of the room, crouching to investigate under the high
shelf of her bed. There’s a smallish wooden crate full of projectors and datapads, another
even smaller box of unrecognizable and probably-worthless trinkets, and a couple dark
canvas pouches attached to a wide belt, with smaller buckling straps that dangle down. He
assumes they’re worn like thigh holsters. When he rifles carefully through one, he finds a few
additional, narrow clamp-vices, more tubes of pigment and glue, and jars of metallic powder.
Inside the other, he finds a series of magnifying glasses and slender brushes, a variety of
metal files, some kind of tool he doesn’t recognize - that’s a first, he thinks, and pockets it -
and the skinniest solder-gun he’s ever seen.



Surprisingly useful, he admits silently, and takes that too.



Then he glances upward and sees a tiny armory of weapons magnet-clasped to the underside
of the bed. He holds back a chuckle of surprised delight. It’s significantly less than what he
might have hoped for, but a lot more than he’d expected. There’s a quad blaster, a selection of
small daggers, a laser pistol, and a smallish electric-bola cannon that he immediately plans to
use on her when it’s time to get rid of her.



She shifts above him and he stills for a moment. She murmurs something, and he sees the
curtain of her hair ripple where it hangs over the edge of the bed. A moment later, the slim
hand he’d seen cradled on her pillow now droops over the shelf of the bed. Her fingers are
still curled delicately, and there’s something about the slender bones in her wrist that just
make him mad.



He thinks of his own mangled paws and wants to bite her. Hard.



His lip peels back in a silent snarl. He waits a beat, then rolls his eyes when she doesn’t stir
again.



He slides soundlessly out from under the shelf-bed. There’s a little table between the head of
the bed and the door, and it’s the only thing he hasn’t checked out yet. A powered-down
plasma lantern perches on it, and he sees a black glass rectangle that he’s sure is full of some
kind of interesting tech he could enjoy breaking into, as well as a tissue-thin scrap of black
cloth. He picks up the silky piece of fabric, and realizes it’s a three-fingered glove. The ends
of the thumb, middle, and forefinger are a little heavier than they should be, weighted down
  by some fine, delicate sensors woven into the material. He’s seen this kind of glove with
  certain screen and projection programs, but he hasn’t had the chance to play with one. He’s
  sure he’d be able to think of something interesting to do with the tiny sensors inside.



  Unfortunately, he suspects that all the tech on her little table - easily the most interesting stuff
  in the ship so far - will be noticed if it goes missing. And he isn’t sure whether she actually
  arms herself every day and will recognize if he steals from her meager armory, or if she’s
  enough of a dumbass that it all just stays under her bed. He’ll find a way to check tomorrow.



  At least now he has a better idea of what he’s dealing with.



  He moves to the door and ducks out as soon as it slides open, making a circuit through the
  other bunks as he heads toward his own. On his way, he snags a number of unused pillows
  and almost every blanket he can find, then chucks them onto the mattress when he gets back
  to his quarters. He remakes the bed to his preferred design - comfortable and soft, like a den
  or a nest. Then he’s finding a suitable length of sheet for his second perch and launching
  himself from floor to desktop to the metal beams interlacing through the ceiling, and he
  begins rigging up a hammock from the sheet.



  He does like a good bed - but tonight, he wants to be high up, with plenty of room. He eases
  himself into the hammock, and stretches out, letting his tail drape over the side: more relaxed
  than he’s been in cycles.



  Yeah. It’s good to be outta that cage, and on his very own ship.

                                   Chapter 2: Monster For A Pet.
Chapter Summary



      in which one hero wrestles with his inner Groot, and the other is quite possibly a moron.



Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes




   Jolie makes coffee in the morning, and rehydrates some egg, which she scrambles with
   powdered milk and a splash of water. There are some spices and dried vegetables she picked
   up in Indigarr on her last trip there, re-illuminating one of their holy texts, and it’s good as
   hell in some rehydrated egg.



   She makes a huge plate of them, then hesitates and checks the food storage locker again.
   Eggs only for this morning, she decides reluctantly. There’s plenty of dried orloni and a
   whole box of egg-mix, but only enough other proteins to get them to Conjunction before
   running out. She suspects her new copilot was half-starved when she fed him yesterday, but if
   he eats like that for much longer, she’ll have to forgo more than a few meals to make the
   protein last.



   There is plenty of fruit to rehydrate though, so she scrubs down the rehydrator plate in the
   sink and then piles it with a medley of stonefruit and pomes, along with some kind of
   aggregate berry that is surprisingly sour. They rotate for a minute in the rehydrator and when
   they’re done, she removes the whole interior plate. A rehydrator plate isn’t meant for eating
   off, the same way that the spinning platter in a microwave back home isn’t meant for dining.
   Unfortunately, Jolie has been solo for a long time, and she’s only needed one plate and a
   couple rounds of silverware - so the rehydrator plate is pulling double-duty right now.



   Desperate times call for desperate measures. Or something.



   It’s a good chunk of time before her new copilot shuffles out into the dining nook. When he
   does, he’s scrubbing his eyes with his forearm, slumping at the bar. Not a morning person,
she notes to herself. She’s already set the two forks on the bartop, so she leans over and grabs
one.



“I hate to tell you this,” she says with mock-regret, “but we’re on limited dishware here,
darling, and I’m not willing to skip two meals in a row. So you’re gonna have to share this
plate with me.”



Something flickers in his eyes but she studiously ignores it, leaning her elbows onto the
countertop to stab a forkful of egg. He hops up onto the barstool, takes the other fork, and
digs in, but she’s pretty sure he’s glowering at her the whole time.



“Coffee or tea?” she offers between bites. “I have one more bottle of greenwine and you’re
welcome to it, but then we’ll be out till Conjunction.”



He doesn’t react at all, just eating and glaring, and she shrugs before plucking up a wedge of
one of the reddish-pink pomes. It snaps in her mouth, sweet and crisp, and she decides to
leave the rest of the eggs to him. He put away a lot of food yesterday, and she’s not sure how
hungry he’ll be today, but she wants to make sure he doesn’t starve. She has no idea what sort
of metabolism he’s working with, and she knows he’s not going to communicate anything he
might actually need to her.



She cleans her mixing bowl in the sonic sink while he finishes the eggs, and she hides a smile
when she turns to take the plate and he’s already handing it to her. Once the dishware and the
rehydrator plate are washed, she seals up the sink and presses the button to heat-sterilize any
remaining contaminants.



And then they’re ready to go.



She’s already noticed that the cage is gone - where he put it, she has no idea. There isn’t even
the ghost of rust on the floor to indicate it was ever in the cockpit. In its absence, she slides
easily into the pilot’s chair and gestures him into the seat next to her. She scans through the
limited selection of music - she only has about twenty-five recordings, though some are
inhumanely long. Music isn’t incredibly easy to access out here - some species have no
interest in it, some just haven’t invested in it, and some find the singularity of live
performances to be a holy and sacrosanct thing. Regardless, finding a new song recording in
the galaxy is way more difficult than she would’ve thought.
The selection she has is, at turns, beautiful, or intriguing, or energizing - but to be honest,
nothing really slaps like the old earth-tunes. She has a few clones of some of Pete’s music,
but it’s not the same as being able to pull up a list of hundreds or even thousands of songs and
listen to whatever takes her mood.



And she misses lyrics.



Nevertheless, it’s better than nothing, so she programs a temporary playlist for the ride.



Flicking on the flight engines, checking her readouts, she says distractedly, “All our bids
were accepted, so we’ll be docking at the Dead Morrigan today and taking a break to sleep
later on an empty moon in the Splinter. Tomorrow we’ll meet up with the Faraday in the
morning, and overnight in an abandoned pocket in the Achaemenid system. Onward to
Conjunction the next day to refuel and get whatever you need. Sound good?”



She doesn’t expect a response and of course, she doesn’t receive one. Once everything is set
on the console, she pauses, rests her wrists across each other on the yoke, and tilts her head
so she can look at her new friend where he sits in the copilot’s chair.



“You don’t happen to fly, too, do you?” she asks on a whim, almost wistful. He seems pretty
at ease in a cockpit, sharp eyes taking everything in, and she imagines that if he hasn’t
already piloted craft in the past, he’s actively learning as she speaks.



Of course he says nothing, looking out into the sky ahead of them, but she can see the corner
of his lip curve in a barely-restrained sneer.



That expression is too complicated to interpret in the context of her question. She chews her
lip, then shrugs and rests one palm on the thruster. “All right, friend. Just let me know if you
want me to turn over the controls.”



They move smoothly from a float into forward flight, and soon the stars and satellites are
zipping by in the distance as they head to the first jump.
She watches him from the corner of her eye. As the hours pass, he relaxes into the chair, and
she’s even more certain that he’s at home behind a flight control panel. When she maneuvers
the Gemma Lynn, his hands twitch, and when they finally get to the first jump, he readies
himself before she even warns him.



 It takes about half a day to get to their destination. The Dead Morrigan is a bit smaller than
she’d expected, though it still dwarfs the Gemma Lynn. Once they’re docked, she stands and
stretches.



“You staying here, or coming with me?” she asks as she makes her way across the ship from
the cockpit to the bay. Sweeping through the common area, she grabs the canvas supply bags
she’d brought from her room earlier in the morning and begins buckling them around her
waist and each thigh. She glances at him where he’s followed her. “It’ll probably be pretty
boring either way,” she says sympathetically.



He seems to consider her words, but doesn’t respond.



“Okay,” she nods. “I should be back and ready to leave in about six hours.”



He stares back unblinkingly.



She hesitates. “Please don’t get in trouble,” she says at last, chewing her lip. “That bounty is
still out for you, and folks on the Dead Morrigan seem potentially shady.”



She hates the act of leaving. But she bites her lip, and makes herself do it anyway.

Rocket happens to know a lot of the crew on the Dead Morrigan - or at least, know of them -
and “shady” is a frickin’ understatement.
Once he’s sure the Terran has left the docking bay, he immediately drops down the hatch to
check the tiny armory under her bed. He’s simultaneously a little gratified - and very
disappointed - to find she’s taken both potentially-lethal firearms and most of the daggers.
The broad is apparently slightly smarter than he’d given her credit for. The Dead Morrigan
crew is overwhelmingly composed of bounty hunters, and he’s tangled with a few of them
before - including swiping some of their pricier targets right out from under them.



He’s not trying to run into a single one of ‘em without being fully decked out in the heaviest
artillery he can get his paws on.



He briefly considers just undocking the Gemma Lynn while the Terran girl is with her, uh,
new employers. It’s an easy solution. He has enough units to refuel the ship on his own and
still get what he needs on Conjunction. And imagining her left to her own devices on the
Dead Morrigan is hysterical. She might be doing some kind of job for them now, but based
on what little he’s gathered, she has no skills she can barter long-term for passage, and barely
any units to her name.



Groot would be disappointed though. He would say something like, she shared her food with
you, or she gave up those units for you.



He growls, mentally glaring at the imaginary Groot. So what?



“I didn’t make her stick her damn nose in. I didn’t make her transfer all those units just so she
could buy a little monster for a pet,” he snarls to no-one. “Her being a narcissistical moron
has got nothin’ to do with me.”



That isn’t fair, he can hear Groot saying reasonably. She was trying to help you.


His mental-Groot has the stupidest voice.


“Too bad,” he snaps out loud. Besides, there’s no reason he ever has to tell Groot about any
of this. Once he gets rid of the Terran and gets Groot out of the Kyln, Rocket can just tell his
friend that he stole the Gemma Lynn.
And it won’t even be a lie, exactly.



He grits his teeth, stalking down to his own bunk, and begins ripping apart every gadget he’s
stolen in the last day. He’s stewing in his anger, letting it build, because anger is familiar and
comfortable. It’s the only thing that’s ever gotten him what he needed.



But it also makes you reckless, some part of him protests. And it also got Teefs and Floor
killed.



He buries that part under daydreams of rubble and gunfire.



Because he refuses to go soft on this broad. He refuses to get tricked, to get sold, to get made
fun of, to get toyed with, to get used. Because ultimately, those things are all the galaxy has
to offer him, aren’t they? Finding a friend in Groot had been a once-in-a-trillion-lifetimes
fluke of the universe - and frankly, a fluke of the Flora Colossus’ own placid, loving
stubbornness - and Rocket knows that even that has never been meant for him, and that he
hasn’t deserved it.



You could figure out the complex workings of cytoplasmic filtration systems, but you couldn't
figure out that?



His heart is thudding against his prosthetic sternum. Trapped. He looks down and sees that at
some point in his frenzy, he’s pieced together four small incendiary devices. Driven by a need
to do something, he tosses them into one of the drawers in his desk-turned-workbench, then
throws himself out into the corridor to begin a new search for anything he’s missed so far.



He searches her room - more thoroughly, but also more recklessly this time. He finds a small
fan in a drawer and he’s not sure what she’s been using it for, but it’s his now: a little trove of
wiring and batteries and belts and blades. He finds a sheaf of delicate, curved knives and fine
razors, bundled into a canvas roll - those are his now, too.
Some small part of him starts to become aware that he’s just revenge-stealing at this point:
yeah, all this stuff will be useful to him, but his driving motivation right now is purely
vindictive. Sure enough, her glove and the black glass rectangle are gone, which means she
probably does take them with her every day - and that’s a frickin’ bummer, because he
would’ve shredded that glove at this point to get at the delicate sensors, and cracked into the
glass to take a peek at the tech inside.



The more he thinks about leaving her behind here, the more impossible it seems. He’d told
himself at first that she has nothing to barter with, but that’s not strictly true, is it? She knows
who he is to the High Evolutionary, and she knows how much money he’s worth. If he
abandons her here, she’ll just tell the crew of the Dead Morrigan about the bounty on his
head, and he’ll be running again in a matter of minutes. At least dropping her on Conjunction
would give him some time to get away. The so-called authorities on Conjunction only really
care about petty bribes and local power struggles, and they don’t waste time pursuing
criminals who’ve already left the planet. That’s why Conjunction is the way it is: a black-
market dream and a den of lowlifes. Like himself.



She could be a new friend, Groot would have said. Our only one in the universe.



It’s enraging all over again. He doesn’t need any new friends, and new friends sure as hell
don’t need him.



Even though he wants this ship - his ship - it suddenly feels like a cage right now. He paces.
He moves every tool from the mechanical room into his bunk. He’d seen a long-nosed lighter
in the kitchen the night before - he goes back, takes that. There’s a manual hand-mixer he can
use the gears from, and he can dismantle at least one igniter from the two-burner stovetop. He
doesn’t care that she seems to use the small electric kettle every day - he cracks into the base,
pulls out the wiring and the heating plate, trundles that up in his arms too. He’s reckless in his
fury, snatching whatever he can get his hands on that won’t make his life harder or his ship
unstable.



When the airlock finally clicks and beeps and whooshes to let the girl in, he’s striding past it
with a pile of kitchen appliances balanced precariously in his arms. She’s laughing sweetly at
whoever’s behind her in the docking bay, saying good-bye with waves that are too joyful,
too generous, like she’s just charmed the entire impossible crew of the Dead Morrigan, and
he hates it so much.
The airlock closes, and she turns, and - welp, there he is, staring back, arms full.



A manual kitchen timer tips and falls out of the crook of his elbow, clattering to the ground
awkwardly.



They both look at it for a moment.



When her eyes flick back to his, he shrugs and opens his arms, letting the entire horde crash
to the floor.



A few circuitry discs go rolling, spinning like coins before falling to their sides.



For a long moment, everything is silent.



“Hello, handsome,” she says casually, conversationally. “Long day?”



++++



She hasn’t asked for any of the stuff back, and he’s left it in a pile where he dropped it. He
doesn’t join her in the cockpit when she maneuvers them away from the Dead Morrigan -
he’s too mad at himself for not taking the chance and leaving her ass.



The way she’d said good-bye to the crew makes him think she would’ve figured out a way to
be just fine, thank you very frickin’ much.



Now, instead, he has to deal with being the butt of her stupid jokes. Plus, he doesn’t think he
can sit in that cockpit for another minute without demanding to take over their flight path to
the Splinter. Her flying is fine, but he’s better - faster, more agile - and more to the point, he
misses it.
Handsome, she’d said. He clenches his fist around the soldergun wrapped in his fingers. He
supposes she thinks she’s frickin’ funny. He also supposes he might end up killing her after

At some point, she must set the Gemma Lynn to autopilot, because she’s tapping at his bunk
door.



He doesn’t respond. He’s filling a drawer with a dozen little bombs, and building the core of
something new - and larger. He’s not sure what it is yet, but it’s gonna be able to blow up
something big. If she leaves his scavenged haul on the floor by the airlock overnight, he’ll
retrieve that stuff too, and he thinks maybe he can pull together something a little more
deadly, a little more fun.



He hears a soft, quiet clatter as she places something on the floor outside the door and he
pauses, listening to her retreat. When he sniffs, there’s a new aroma that makes his stomach

There’s the singular plate, piled high with rehydrated Moraggian moonfish, grilled and
seasoned. There are cold slices of yaro root brined with Xandaran dewhoney, and wedges of
rehydrated frostmelon. A glass of water, a chipped Xandaran breakfast-cup of curlflower tea
that has turned a creamy pinkish-gold with whatever milk and sweetener she’s added, and the
remaining bottle of Contraxian greenwine.



He has got to get rid of her.



It’s only another rotation and a half till Conjunction - only a rotation and a half of having to
deal with her, he reasons. He can do that. Then he’ll get what he needs, take the Gemma
Lynn, and be gone. She’d mentioned having a longer job there, so she’ll at least have some
resources and some contacts to take care of herself.



Even Groot can’t complain about that, Rocket thinks, and tries to settle back into his
tinkering.

He lunges awake, nearly flipping himself out of the hammock as his heart hammers into his
metal sternum. He can’t breathe. He’s going to die. He can feel it. Here in the dark, alone but
surrounded by ghosts, his heart is going to bash itself to bits against the unbreakable ribcage
implanted inside him.



And he deserves it.



For a second, he tears frantically at his fur, at his skin, trying to rip it out of his chest himself.



He can’t, so he settles for tipping out of the hammock, smashing down to the floor onto his
chest and one forearm. The impact jars all the joints in his twisted-and-pinned body and
knocks the air out of his lungs, but the cold floor feels good on his hot, furred face and
mangled forepaws. He presses into it, fists curled so tight that his claws sink into his palms.
His heart smashes again and again into the unforgiving ground.



My fault.



Slowly, slowly, his pulse eases. Maybe it’s minutes, or maybe it’s hours. Finally, he half-sits,
and scrubs one hand roughly down his wet face, trying to pull the rest of the sweat and heat
and tears out of himself.



He prefers the nights when Vim and Theel and the High Evolutionary are ripping his body
apart and replacing every piece of him with ugliness and pain, because then he just wakes up
afraid and alone and hurting.



The nights with Lylla and Floor and Teefs, though… these nights open up that splinteringly
hollow crack inside him. It feels like he has a gravity bomb planted in his chest. Everything is
empty and sucking and he is always afraid, each time, that it’s going to swallow him whole
and he’ll never be able to close it again.



Either way, though, he hates himself.



Monster.



He sits back for a moment, pulling in breaths he knows he doesn’t deserve. He needs a
shower. And then he needs to…make another bomb, or something. Anything to get rid of this
nausea and this gaping maw of starving, hateful emptiness behind his sternum. Slowly, he
drags himself to his feet, slapping his palm against the panel by the door so it slides open.



When he steps into the corridor, half-lit for the manufactured sleep cycle, something seems
off.



For a second, he tells himself he’s just being paranoid. Sometimes, on nights like these, he
feels panicked and watchful whenever he crosses a threshold. His eyes scan the space though,
and it only takes a second to spot the Terran’s bunk a couple feet away, door wide open.



His blood chills for a second. He approaches cautiously, and sniffs the doorway.



She’s not in there.

He slides through the shadows, swiping the quadblaster from under her bed. All her weapons
are still down there. Swiftly, he darts down the corridor, ears pricked forward and nose on
high-alert. There’s no sign of her - or of anything else - throughout the belly of the Gemma
Lynn, and his heart is hammering all over again.
Up the ladder he goes, silent and shadow-footed past the airlock and his abandoned pile of
scavenged wires and tech. Everything seems quiet - which, in his experience, is when
everything is at its most dangerous. When his eyes scan the tiny common area and
kitchenette, he can see a soft golden glow coming from the cockpit. He approaches slowly,
tense and tight, fingers itching on both triggers of the quadblaster.



When he gets to the edge of the bridge, he sees her.



She’s perched in the pilot’s chair, a holovid projected in a panorama around her. The back of
her head is silhouetted against the luminous view, and in spite of the infinite blackness just
beyond, the world in front of her is made up of copper sunshine and late afternoons. She’s
wrestled her hair into some kind of fastening on the top of her head, and it hangs down in a
long, sleek tail over one shoulder. A few other streamers have escaped, and are looping down
the sides of her bare throat and shoulders. He can see the pearls of her spine at the base of her
neck.



Her hand hovers over the datapad propped up in front of her, fingers encased in the three-
sensored half-glove he’d found two nights ago by her bed.



His breathing eases, every muscle slackening as he lowers the weapon, leaving only vague
agitation and annoyance behind in his body. What the hell is she doing, anyway? It’s an
absurd hour for a humie to be awake.



He looks down at the quadblaster in his hands. He clearly doesn’t need it now, but he doesn’t
want to leave it behind either. What’s he gonna do, toss it in the sonic sink?



For some reason, turning around and leaving doesn’t even enter his mind. Maybe she won’t
notice, he thinks doubtfully, and moves forward. He can’t help his innate curiosity.



He wants to see what exactly she’s looking at.



It takes a moment, but he realizes as he approaches that she’s painting - with light. The wide
white sleeves of her shirt - even more massive and swallowing on her frame than her normal
tunic - are rolled and cuffed halfway up her forearms. She uses the sensors on her thumb and
fingers to zoom in close on the face of another Terran humie: a kid, really, round-cheeked and
freckled.



A brush of the broad’s index finger, and the portrait’s face is colored with the orange-pink
blush of a faint sunburn. She slides her two fingers to the left and the face turns - she cocks
her head, hesitates, and shifts a constellation of freckles on the left cheek, then shakes her
head and slides it back.



He’s next to her now, almost without realizing it, and he tilts his own head as he watches. The
painting looks almost real, like a holovid of an actual person. But the edges are softer, and
here and there he can pick up a brushstroke, or a line that’s too delicate and pretty to be real.



He’s not any kind of artist. He doesn’t know anything about that kind of stuff and he doesn’t
really care, not unless he can steal something that will get a good price. The idea of it - this
highbrow, shit-eating study of beauty and ugliness - leaves him feeling bitter and mean. He
supposes he’s had enough of arrogant jackasses pursuing perfection.



But…there’s something about this thing she’s making. It twists his guts up inside, the way
only certain songs have before. It sounds cheesy and he hates it, but there’s some kind of
feeling in the brushstrokes, bright and bittersweet. It’s weird - the kid looks so mischievous,
so frickin’ innocent and stupid-happy, but something about the way the hair is falling into its
eyes makes his bones ache with the memories of everything he’s lost.



This stupid painted kid makes him think of Floor, of Teefs, of Lylla. All gone. His heart’s
suddenly in his mouth.



Jolie slides her first two fingers left on the screens again and the image spins: now they’re
seeing the back of the kid’s head. She does something with her whole, gloved hand: like a
soft opening, like letting go of a bird. The three sensors in her glove skate outward and away
from each other on the screen.



In response, the image suddenly widens into a broad bronze landscape, fieldgrasses and trees
all around them, and the kid’s whole body is there in front of them. It’s a coltish, childish
Terran girl with knobby knees and teeth just a little too big for her face. She moves in the
shifting meadow, looking back over her shoulder and laughing soundlessly at Rocket before
running away into the tall golden grass. He can almost feel the leaves whisper against each
other. The kid’s copper hair ripples behind her, and then the painting dissolves into amber
mist.



Jolie hasn’t taken her eyes off the screens, but the broad has to know he’s here. He glances up
at her, wondering who the kid is - almost impulsively blowing his already-questionable cover
and opening his mouth to ask - and then the twist in his gut vanishes in favor of his stomach
suddenly dropping right through his feet. He freezes.



Jolie’s cheek and the line of her throat are both slick with reflected light. Her eyes are silver-
rimmed - bright - with the lashes all starred out in dampness.



He watches as her shoulders buckle upward in a movement he recognizes all too well: it’s the
involuntary motion that comes with grappling a sob into silence. Her throat works, but her
gaze doesn’t waver.



No sound escapes her body.



He doesn’t like this. He doesn’t like this at all. Against his will, his ears drop back, tail
flickering briefly between his ankles in distress. She’s still just sitting there: eyes on the now-
pale light, her face and neck and collarbone all gleaming with tears.



His throat tightens in the dark and he looks away, suddenly uncertain.



He hears her shift, and when he glances back up, she’s looking down at him. He sees her eyes
clock the blaster, but she doesn’t seem fazed by it. Her wet eyes are just soft - so soft - and
she wrings out a lopsided half-smile for him.



“Hey,” she says, her voice curling around him with such a gentleness that it makes his ears
drop further. “Couldn’t sleep?”



What to say to that?
Even if he was willing to tip his hand and talk to her - which he’s not - there aren’t any good
words. And even if there were, he’s bad at using them. He’d probably just say something
cutting and mean.



And…that’s not what he wants right now.



“Do you need anything?” she asks, and she doesn’t sound like she’s been weeping alone in
the dark. Her voice is just quiet, and patient, and maybe a little curious. “What can I do?”



He feels like shit. He’s tired, he’s just spent a fuckton of adrenaline on his own dreams and
fears, and now - this. He doesn’t really wanna examine the weird sense of recognition he’s
experiencing right now, but he doesn’t particularly want to go back to his dark bunk and the
ghosts, either.



Instead, he just looks down at the quadblaster in his hands, and sets it on the console. Then he
hoists himself into the copilot’s seat, and he looks out into the black sky. She’s silent for a
moment, watchful. He ignores her, and eventually, she leans back and taps a few buttons. The
projected light disappears, leaving them with an unobstructed view of the sea of endless
night.



Forever, and beautiful, he thinks, staring out at the darkness, pinpricked by sharp stars.



For a very long time, they simply sit together: silent, and miserable.



But not alone.

little arsenal into the extra pockets, hidden loops, and holsters in his jumpsuit. He snags one
