Chapter Summary



      in which our heroes get fucked. Not in the good way.



Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes



   Jolie hadn’t been able to hear exactly what Rocket had been yelling about in the common
   room a few rotations earlier, but she’s grateful to not have had to navigate Drax, Gamora, and
   Quill fighting over her head since then. It had felt - ominous. Weighty. She could feel it
   pushing down on the crown of her head, compressing all the vertebrae in her spine.

   Reducing her.

   Then they’d filtered out of the cockpit almost organically - taking their complaints to her
   copilot, her secret-hero. He’d yelled whatever-he’d-yelled, and now - well, she wouldn’t say
   the tension has eased, exactly, but it seems like everyone is being more or less civil. Drax, at
   least, seems mollified, and without him paddling against the current, the whole little band of
   misfits collectively breathes more easily.

   Regardless of whatever wisdom or degradation Rocket had heaved at them, they’d fallen
   quiet. When the hero-in-question himself had entered the cockpit looking grumpier than
   usual and tossed a pack of zargnuts at her head, she hadn’t said anything - just caught his eye
   and gave him her most-grateful smile.

   She could tell the second he clocked it because his eyes immediately shifted to the flight
   controls and he’d scoffed at nothing.

   Jolie had already been planning on avoiding any mention of their sleeping together again -
   but now that impulse is reaffirmed and she blesses her instincts once more. She refuses to
   give Rocket even the faintest inclination toward self-consciousness, or to make him think that
   he shouldn’t feel welcome to share the bed whenever he feels like it.

   She wants him there as often as he’s willing to join her.

   And she’d be lying if she didn’t admit - at least to herself - that the want had only grown
   stronger since she’d stretched herself awake this morning only to find him tucked against her
   breasts like the softest semi-circle croissant. She’s pretty sure she’s never seen him so utterly
   relaxed: nose twitching, those fluffy-looking ears at rest, the soft fabric of his pants riding
   low at the base of his spine where his legs curled up and into his abdomen.
The tip of his tail, feathering drowsily against the skin just inside the half-unbuttoned collar
of her shirt.

Jolie had held her breath, trying not to react until she’d been able to ease herself away and off
the foot of the bed.

She’d gotten in the shower and had considered, briefly, releasing some of the shivery-silver
tension that had been building in her abdomen and between her thighs. But she’d just known
she’d be thinking about him, and it felt weird to think about someone - someone who’d never
asked to be the subject of her fantasies and would probably have been appalled by them -
while getting herself off.

Sooner or later, this tension will build to the point where she does it anyway, she thinks. Not
intentionally. She’ll try to think about anything but him - she just knows it’s not gonna work.
Today will not be the day she gives in, however. Instead, she resolutely turns off the heating
lamps, cranks up the cooling fans, and takes the coldest sonic shower of her life.

It only takes minutes for her to decide, teeth chattering, that moral convictions are fucking
stupid.

Still. It seems that not-bringing-up Rocket’s midnight decision to join her in their little nest is
the right call. There’s no way to say it, Jolie thinks, other than that she is rewarded for her
discretion. In the rotations that follow, when she wakes just enough to shift and shuffle her
limbs into sleepy new positions, her fingers find fur every time: Rocket’s warmth and the soft
placid hush of his breathing, curled into a contented crescent under their shared tangle of
covers, pressed into her thigh or flank or belly. He doesn’t join her till after she’s fallen
asleep, and he’s often gone before she fully wakes, but to stir and find him in the middle of
her hazy dreams is a gift.

If she’s supposed to be counting her blessings, she guesses she should be grateful that - as far
as she can tell - there haven’t been any other times when they might’ve been in a
compromising position. The cost of making him uncomfortable is too high to risk that again,
though apparently she has no such qualms with torturing herself.

And so this is how the space between Knowhere and Asgard unfolds: the coziest, rosiest
nights she’s had in years - decades, probably, if she wants to waste time doing the math - and
days spent cascading through jump-points like honeycombs and stardust like spilt glitter.
Snacks tossed at her head by a grumpy copilot who she’s basically-desperately-in-love-with-
shhhh, and the clinking of his inventions, and an uncountable number of golden-hearted
flowers in her hair. And the fragile beginnings of - well, maybe they’d all still disagree and
say Jolie, you moron, this is an uneasy alliance at best - but she’s going to call it a family and
let the word curl up like a kitten in her heart.

She suspects that Groot, at least, would agree with her in this.

When they finally reach the pocket of starry galaxy that cradles the Realm Eternal - hung like
an island in the sky, like a more-feral version of the Neverland she’d seen painted in books as
a kid - Pete slows the Gemma Lynn to a crawl, and Jolie slides into the copilot’s seat.
She calls in a formal request to Heimdall, asking for permission to land. In her experience,
he’s likely already noticed that they are on their way, and may even have picked up on why
they’re here. Asgard still has traditional comms, specifically for sending outgoing
transmissions to the admittedly-rare space travelers who approach Asgard through traditional,
non-Bifrost means. Usually, Heimdall uses them to offer her a warm - if somewhat
intimidating - greeting, and to confirm landing instructions. The gatekeeper typically grants
her access to touch down on the Rainbow Bridge so he can confirm everything is above-
board, so to speak, then has her relocate to a landing field on Asgard-proper. In the past, a
handful of the Queen’s ladies - sometimes even Frigga herself - would meet Jolie there, but
since this visit is unplanned, she’s not sure what to expect.

“Heimdall, this is Jolie of Terra on the Gemma Lynn. I have a crew with me this time - we’re
a group of six. We’re seeking an urgent audience with Her Highness Queen Frigga or the
Allfather on a matter of utmost importance - “ she grins a little “- as I’m sure you know.
Permission to land?”

The comms crackle. From behind her, Rocket pauses in his tinkering and looks up as the
silence continues. Pete’s brow furrows and Jolie feels her little grin fading. Only Drax, who
has been lurking on the bridge all day, seems unperturbed.

“Weird,” Jolie utters, and leans toward comms again, repeating her message. “We’re
requesting landing access,” she says again. “We have an urgent request that we need to relay
to the Allfather. We’re bringing news that has the potential to impact the entire galaxy,
including the Nine Realms.” She hesitates. “We should arrive in twenty.”

There’s still no response, and she feels her brow crease with worry and her shoulders twist up
into her jawline. She’s been out here at least a dozen times, and Heimdall has never not
responded to her.

The crystalline Rainbow Bridge appears to be open and waiting for them when they land, but
as soon as they open the docking bay, step out, and stretch cautiously - Asgardian air always
smells better, Jolie thinks - there’s some sort of flurry of activity in the observatory. A pale,
bald man in dark armor stumbles out, running toward them. Jolie holds up a hand to her
friends, cautioning them, her brow furrowed.

Her gut is fluttering, and not in the nervous-but-golden way she associates with jump-points,
new art, and Rocket. Nope. When she looks around, it feels like there’s a thin gray film
between her and the rest of the world. Everything is happening from a distance and she can
see each piece slotting together, but she can’t catch even a glimpse of the whole picture yet.

Somehow, she just knows that it is going to be ugly.

“Well, you’re not Heimdall,” she says, channeling her best, most-pleasant customer-service
voice as the man reaches them and crouches, hands on his knees as he pants breathlessly.

“Uhm, no,” the man says. His head is tattooed, and he looks vaguely….shifty. The distinct
odor of mead and stale, mediocre sex hovers around him, crowding out all the sparkling
Asgardian sweetness. Jolie sees Gamora flinch and Drax cover his nose out of the corner of
her eye, and Quill looks positively queasy. Only Groot seems unphased.
“Yeesh,” Rocket mutters behind her, never one to hide his disparaging opinions. “Sorta
underwhelming performance from the Asgardian Welcoming Committee.”

Normally, she’d try not to chuckle at that - attempt to play the diplomat, and spare this
stranger’s feelings. But the residue of wrongness locks any real mirth off her lips. Laughing is
not even a temptation.

“Name’s Skurge,” the man wheezes, still hunched. “Heimdall’s replacement.”

Jolie blinks. “Is he okay?”

Skurge gathers up his breaths from where they’ve been dropped on the bridge beneath their
feet. “He was found t’be a traitor to Asgard. Neglectful of his duties. Odin banished ‘im.”

Jolie’s eyes narrow. “That is…surprising.” Heimdall - neglectful? Treacherous? No. More
pieces slide into place, clicking like pins in an impossible lock that she’s trying to pick. It’s
all even more troublesome, given that the Gemma Lynn had fully landed and they’d all
disembarked right onto the bridge before this… guy… had even realized something was
going on.

“Well. Skurge. It’s certainly something to meet you,” she says politely.

Skurge blinks like he’s sure he’s been insulted but doesn’t know how.

She doesn’t so much bury her misgivings - instead, she gilds them. Smiles again. Deadens
her eyes.

“My name is Jolie and this is the… crew of the Gemma Lynn. I’ve visited quite a few times
in the past? For art assessment, exports, and conservation. Today, uh, we’re here on a
different, urgent…mission, I guess. For the safety of the Nine Realms and the entire galaxy,
we need an emergency audience with the Allfather. I know you don’t know me, but I’ve
worked with the Queen a handful of times, and she can vouch for me.”

“Ah,” Skurge says, and a flicker of true remorse flashes across his face. “You haven’t heard.
Queen Frigga has left us for the halls of Valhalla.”

Jolie’s heart plummets into her boots and stays there, invisible blood seeping right through
her soles and into the shimmering crystal. The news is a doubled-up kick in the teeth, because
the Queen has always been one of Jolie’s favorite fucking people in this galaxy - never mind
the fact that they’d really only met each other on a dozen or so occasions.

It’s just that Jolie has so often thought about how lucky Thor and Loki were - to have such a
mother.

The second kick-in-the-mouth is that Frigga had been their best fucking hope of convincing
someone with both a record of actual personal responsibility and the disproportional power
needed to take this terrifying purple weapon of mass destruction off their hands.

Still, Jolie draws in a shaky breath and tries to remember the formal, traditional condolences.
“May she live long in the memory of the people of Asgard, and sit ever among her kinsfolk
in Valhalla,” she says, and means it. “I praise her for the greatness of her character, for the
steadfastness of her courage, and for the wisdom of her bright spirit.”

Skurge nods, his eyes dimmed by something that might actually be sorrow - surprising, but a
better sign than Jolie was beginning to hope for. He offers, “I can still, uh, announce you to
the Allfather. What did you want me to tell him again?”

“We want to give you the power stone,” Drax speaks up, and Gamora elbows him roughly.

“What’s wrong with you?” Jolie hears Pete hiss. “You’ve been squirrelly all day.”

Rocket just sighs, and even Groot grunts a little from where he stands.

Jolie closes her eyes for a minute. If this fuckin’ Kylosian weren’t so damn lovable, she’d -

“I am not a squirrel,” Drax says, affronted.

Jolie sighs, opens her eyes, and drags up a smile for the Asgardian sky before turning her
gaze back down to Skurge.

“I know the Allfather keeps a lot of rare - and in many cases, dangerous - relics in his vaults,”
she says. “We were hoping to… “ She hesitates. “To consult.”

“And maybe get some help covering costs,” Pete pipes up, and Rocket rumbles an agreement.
“You know, of travel and…things.”

Jolie tries not to roll her eyes. Speaking of lovable idiots. Gamora elbows him as well,
hissing something under her breath.

Skurge has already perked up, though. “Oh, the Allfather will be very interested to hear about
a… a power stone,” he says earnestly. “Let’s go.”

Jolie brow creases and she hums skeptically. “You’re going to…take us to him? Yourself?”

“Aren’t you supposed to guard this bridge or something?” Rocket adds, stamping one foot on
the crystalline structure and watching curiously as iridescence radiates outward from the
pressure. Jolie can tell he’s trying to figure out what it’s made from, how it reacts, and if he
can snatch a piece of it. Worthy wondering, she supposes - but right now she’s wishing he
would turn that awesome brainpower toward figuring out whatever it is that’s got her feeling
so much dread.

“Shouldn’t you also be here to open the Bifrost if someone needs it?” she asks Skurge, still
trying to parse it all out. “Not to mention…don’t you want us to move our ship?”

For a moment, Skurge looks conflicted, then shakes it off like a dog. “I’m sure it’s fine,” he
says uncertainly, and turns to lead the way.

Christ, this guy is not helping put her mind at ease. Jolie bites her lip, then exchanges looks
with her adopted family. “Whatever I thought was weird before is getting weirder,” she
confesses under her breath. “Should we - “ she winces. “Do we need to, like, abort, abort?”
She’s so mad at herself for even suggesting it, but even the blue sky looks threatening right
now.

“No,” Drax replies immediately, surprising her. He does look…squirrelly. Anxious, maybe?

“If even you’re getting the spooky-ookies - “ she starts.

“No,” he repeats. “We have traveled too long to leave right away.”

It’s not anxiety. Jesus Christ, what is going on? “Are you okay?” Jolie murmurs to the
Kylosian.

“You comin’?” asks Skurge, already partway down the bridge.

Drax grunts. “I will stay with the Gemma Lynn,” he says firmly. “You all go. Find out if the
stone can be safely kept here.”

“I am Groot,” offers Groot.

“Maybe leave the stone with Drax?” Pete asks the group under his breath. “Because, yeah,
I’ve never been here and even I can tell something’s up.”

“This doesn’t read right,” Jolie says, pathetically. But Gamora’s nodding and honestly,
Rocket just looks fuckin’ bored, so she watches - helpless and without anything to back up
her instincts - as Pete flips his jacket open and stealthily passes the orb to Drax.

“Well?” Skurge calls, sounding impatient and distressed all at once.

So Jolie puts one boot in front of the other, and walks into Asgard with her friends.

++++

The closer they get to the core of Asgard, the more Jolie’s heart crawls up her chest cavity
and then into her mouth. It folds itself onto her tongue, swollen and dangerous.

She remembers a book she’d read just after undergrad. It had told her that gut instinct and
intuition aren’t based on nothing: they’re a survival mechanism so old there isn’t a name for
the sixth sense of it. The animal-brain catches information too swift and subtle for the
philosopher-brain to parse through: the brief scent of the tiger in the reeds, the fleeting
expression of contempt on a lover’s face. Jolie wonders what information is slipping past her
logic right now, pinging that prehistoric radar in her vagus nerve.

There is no misreading or dismissing Odin’s glance of contempt, though. The condescension
ripples off him and trails on the pavers of the courtyard, caught in the folds at the end of his
robes.

He isn’t anything like Jolie expected. If she ignores his transparent disdain, she can see he’s
clearly in the midst of revelry and possibly a great deal of semipublic sexual debauchery.
And, okay, when she’s at her best, Jolie’s not one to kinkshame - but it seems like he should
still be mourning Frigga. She tries to squash down the shiver of resentment clawing its way
up her spine to match fists with the pure creeping terror she’s feeling in every moment since
she first sent that message to Heimdall. A person’s gotta grieve however they gotta grieve,
she tells herself.

But shouldn’t he be doing kingly, godly, Allfathery stuff during business hours or something?
Frigga had made it seem like he’d grown wiser over the centuries: more patient, more
thoughtful.

“Maybe this was a mistake,” she utters again under her breath to Rocket, who’s currently
peering around the courtyard in disgust. “I… misjudged. I misjudged. Fuck. We should go?”
She feels so defeated and honestly, scared, a panicked little animal in a trap. It must leak into
her voice, because her copilot shoots her a disgruntled look.

“No,” he reminds her. “You didn’t misjudge. Somethin’s weird. You noticed before we even
landed. But - “ He shrugs. “We all decided to check it out.”

He’s right. Of course he’s right.

But something still crawls under her fingernails, between her teeth. She’s missed something.
She’s forgotten something. She’s left the oven on at home.

Now her laughter comes, and she stomps on the nervous giggle that billows up in her throat
like a sickly cloud of steam. The effort’s wasted: the sound gets stuck behind her thudding,
swollen heart anyway.

The Allfather in question remains supremely annoyed as soon as he gestures away the actors
and groupies lounging with him. He beckons Skurge, hissing something about guarding the
bridge in case Thor returns.

Jolie’s mind rakes at that, tries to grip it and turn it over and examine it. Is this the missing
piece of the puzzle, the final pin in the lock? She knows the two Odinsson boys are a handful,
but have things gotten worse?

“I know, I know,” says Skurge, “but they said they wanted to bring you - I think the big one
called it a power stone?”

Odin blinks, and his frustration melts away. He gives Skurge one last dirty glare - “Get back
to the observatory and let me know if anyone else decides to make an appearance “ - and then
turns back to them with a winning smile on his soft, elderly face.

“That seems like trouble,'' Rocket mutters, and Jolie knows he’s referring to Odin’s sudden
change of mood upon hearing what they’ve brought to Asgard.

“The vibes are not great,” she agrees in a whisper, and prides herself on the understatement of
the year.

“Greetings - ahem - seasoned travelers,” the Allfather says jovially, and Jolie winces at the
not-so-subtle jab at their grubbiness compared to the clean splendor of Asgard. Skurge is
slinking off, like a dog with his tail between his legs - and Jolie is still missing something.
“I am Groot,” says Groot, and Odin waves a benevolent hand.

“Welcome, welcome, yes. I am Odin, Allfather of Asgard.” He reaches out and links his arm
with Gamora’s, patting her hand in a way that maybe should seem grandfatherly, but doesn’t.
“Tell me what I can do for you.”

Gamora hesitates - thank god Jolie isn’t crazy, thank god Gamora has clearly picked up on
the weirdness too. Even Pete seems a little distrustful at this point.

“Well,” the assassin says slowly, “as…Skurge has mentioned, we have an infinity stone.
Ronan the Accuser has been pursuing it on behalf of Thanos, and we’d hoped that the vaults
of Asgard might be a place where it can be contained and kept safe from those with nefarious
purposes. As I’m sure you can imagine -“ Gamora adds hastily “- for Thanos or Ronan to get
their hands on this stone could only cause misery for the entire universe, including the Nine
Realms.”

Odin chuckles, and the sound is uncomfortably dark and knowing. Abort, abort! Jolie thinks
again.

“Oh, I can imagine quite well,” the Allfather tells them.

Gamora’s face is closing up now. “Perhaps we shouldn’t have bothered you with this,
Allfather. We know of another organization that might -“

“Of course you should have,” Odin interrupts, his voice expansive and a bit too generous, too
generous. “The power stone will absolutely be in safe hands here. I’ll see to it that it is tucked
away safely in our vault, under the fiercest of guardianship, and I will personally oversee its
protection. What do you need in return, so that you may go back to your lives?”

Rocket’s ears tilt forward at that, but Jolie’s stomach drops.

“Now that you mention it,” Rocket starts, but Pete’s intervening.

“Uh, I changed my mind actually. I think I’m with Gamora on this one,” her fellow Terran
says abruptly. “We shouldn’t be bringing anyone else into this. It was a mistake to try to -“

“Really, dude?” Rocket’s complaining, exasperated.

Jolie’s eyes dart to each of them, one by one, trying to figure out what she isn’t seeing.

“Nonsense,” the Allfather interrupts, and his eyes twinkle as if he’s enjoying this exchange.
“Come. What would you have in return for your great service to the universe?”

“What service is that, Father?” asks a new, deeper, angrier voice, and Jolie watches Odin’s
face pale before the newcomer enters their view.

He’s tall, broad, and golden. Thor, her mind supplies immediately. She’s never met him, but
even if addressing Odin as father hadn’t given him away, how could anyone who’d heard of
him not recognize him?
She holds her breath, and hopes. Maybe this is the answer.

Odin stumbles a bit over his words. “Ah, my favorite son,” he greets, though it sounds like
his teeth are clenched. “These travelers come bearing a gift -“

“More like a curse,” Jolie murmurs without thinking, and she’s as surprised by the words as
her copilot, who’s flashing her a look that’s halfway to concern.

“Well, yes, I suppose one could see it that way, if not for the great safety that my
guardianship will offer the galaxy and the Nine Realms,” Odin reminds her. His voice is pure
annoyance.

“Allow me to introduce myself,” the elder Odinsson directs to their little group, with an edge
to his voice that Jolie feels sure is all for his father. “My name is Thor Odinsson, God of
Thunder and future King of Asgard. What is it you bring to my father to protect the galaxy
and Nine Realms?”

“An infinity stone,” Gamora supplies readily, apparently - like Jolie - thinking that this prince
might be a better ally than his father after all.

Thor’s eyebrows flare upwards. “An infinity stone?” he turns to his father. “And you’re
hoping to keep it here, Father? Truly?”

“You know, I didn’t expect you to return to Asgard so quickly, my son. And so…
unannounced.”

“Yes, well, heard that the Avengers may have found my idiot-brother’s brainwashing-scepter,
and I thought I’d let you know before I went to make sure it didn’t do any more damage,”
Thor is drawling. He sounds pissed. “I had a bit of a time getting the Bifrost to open. Any
idea why that might be?”

Odin chuckles weakly. “Well, my son -“

“And why you’re accepting another infinity stone, when just last year you ordered Lady Sif
and the Warriors Three to remove the reality stone from Asgard, so that we could keep it at a
great distance from the tesseract?”

“I wish I had a snack,” Rocket is telling Groot.

“I am Groot.”

“Wait, you had another infinity stone?” Gamora says, confused, at the same time Jolie’s
asking, “The tesseract?”

Thor looks at them both, impatience warring with well-trained chivalry. “Yes. We protect the
tesseract in our vault. We know it houses an infinity stone - the space stone. We came into
possession of the reality stone recently, and - knowing how dangerous it might be to keep two
stones in close proximity - my dear father ordered the reality stone to be taken to the other
side of the galaxy.”
“Seems weird to change his mind now,” Rocket deadpans, and surely - surely, Jolie thinks -
this must be the thing crawling across her scalp, setting all her little hairs acrackle.

“Indeed, wise rabbit,” Thor agrees. Rocket falters, then looks flattered - almost preening - but
before anyone can say anything more, Thor is lifting his father by the robes, shaking him for
good measure. “Isn’t it odd, father?”

“Okay! Okay.” Odin lifts his hands in surrender, his voice a little higher, less gravelly, more
silky - and annoyed. “Put me down, you brute.”

Thor just shakes him again and Pete’s trying to tentatively intervene, saying, “Look, we’re
not necessarily opposed to brutalizing the elderly, but the elderly have to really deserve it - “

Whatever glamour was around the Allfather slowly dissolves, revealing a slender man with
dark, sleek hair and a hunted look in his eyes, hanging from Thor’s massive fists.

“Well, that’s new,” offers Rocket, nonplussed.

“Meet my brother, Loki Odinsson,” Thor says through gritted teeth.

“Laufeyson,” Loki corrects, but it’s clear his heart isn’t in it. Thor scoffs and drops him
abruptly, and the trickster stumbles, and Jolie breathes a sigh of relief because this makes
sense now and everything is fine.

“Where is Father?”

“Wouldn’t you like to know?”

“Where is he?”

“I exiled him to your beloved Terra!”

“Wow,” says Pete.

“You guys got issues,” Rocket’s adding, sounding legitimately perturbed.

But it still doesn’t feel fine. Jolie clenches her jaw and retreats again into full dead-eyed,
customer-service smile, waving one hand at the brothers to get their attention. “Yes, hello,
thank you, this is all very fucked, but we are trying to hide an infinity stone.”

Thor sighs and turns back to her, his face already apologetic.

“By the way,” she adds grimly, still groping in the dark for the hidden safety latch, the thing
that will make it all make sense, the thing that will stop this nervous twist in her belly. “You
didn’t happen to drop off that reality stone with Taneleer Tivan, did you?”

Gamora sucks in a breath and even Rocket jolts a little, and now Thor looks suddenly
worried. He’s scanning them, looking for a hidden trick or ulterior motives, before he
reluctantly offers, “Yes…?”
“Mmhm,” is all Jolie can bring herself to say. Her mouth is sour. “Well, if you’re not going to
take the power stone, we need to go elsewhere,” she tells him, trying to make her voice firm.
Strong. “We have one place in mind where it might be safe. But if you have other
suggestions…?”

Thor’s already shaking his head. “The Collector was our best wager in protecting the reality
stone,” he says darkly, “though I am interpreting from your statement that it was not a wise
one.”

“In some ways, I guess that remains to be seen,” Gamora fills in, “but he was… eager to get
his hands on the power stone too.”

“We’ll be happy to get out of your hair,” Rocket interjects reasonably. “But it cost us a lot to

“Rocket,” Jolie admonishes. God, she’s already so tired. And mad at herself - for making

“What?” he asks, all innocence. “I’m just wondering if our new, uh, allies wanna offer us any

“Of course,” Thor intervenes smoothly, and his hand reaches out almost nonchalantly to

Where will you be headed?”

Jolie looks to Gamora, who looks almost as wrung-out as Jolie feels. “Back to Xandar, I

“Xandar is a good choice,” Thor confirms, nodding thoughtfully. “The Nova Corps are
valiant and will protect it with their lives.”

“They may have to,” Gamora murmurs grimly.

“Yeah, well, we could do with some artillery, too,” Rocket interrupts, gazing up at Thor. “Just

“I assume you must be the weaponsmaster, then,” Thor says with a deferential nod, and
Rocket’s chest puffs up again.

“I am, actually, yes.” A pause. “And possibly also the captain. We’re still working on that
one.”

Another thing Jolie would’ve laughed at - would’ve reveled in the flickering warmth of - if
she wasn’t feeling so nauseous.

“I am happy to show you some of our finer armaments,” Thor is telling Rocket
conversationally. “Unfortunately, most of them are built for gods. Your small body will lack
the strength to wield the majority of them.”

Rocket’s ears twitch. “I’m stronger than I look - “

Thor’s already shaking his head. “I mean no insult, Captain. Only that you are not a god.
Even the strongest mortal form would simply crumble upon wielding such a weapon - even
as your mind collapsed into madness.”

Rocket pauses and reconsiders. “Is it bad that that kinda makes me wanna do it more?”

Jolie rubs her temples. Christ. She has the world’s worst headache.

“We can still look,” Thor is telling Rocket kindly. “Please follow me. We’ll set you up with
the finest Asgardian hospitality for the night, while I torture my brother to find out where on

“Also, I met your fine friend out by your ship. He was similarly hoping for access to

“Really?” Rocket asks, bemused, and Thor nods as he begins to lead the way into the vaulted
halls.

“I had asked him to relocate to the landing fields, and he said he could do so in short order - “

“That jackass better not be tryin’ to fly my ship - “

“ - as soon as the party you are waiting on arrives.”

Jolie freezes, her mouth pulling into something between a frown and a sob, and she hazards a
horrified glance at the others.

It wasn’t anxiety, she thinks.

“I am Groot?”

Both Thor and Loki whip their heads around to stare at the Flora Colossus, twin looks of
horror spilling across their very different features.

“No way,” Rocket is telling his friend. “There’s no way Drax -“

It was anticipation.

Jolie’s ears pop suddenly - painfully - like vast amounts of air have just been displaced, and
there is a low, rumbling boom that shakes the ground beneath their feet.

“What - ?”

“I am Groot.”

Thor’s already turning, gazing in the direction of the crystalline bridge, but nothing is visible
from here. He grips the trickster by the throat. “We are not done, brother,” he growls, and
then launches into the air, led by Mjolnir.

“Uh, we follow, right?” asks Pete, but Rocket’s already cursing. His eyes are furious.

“Groot think Drax sent a transmission to Ronan before we left the Tranta system,” he says.

Jolie doesn’t wait for him to finish. “We’ve gotta get to the Gemma Lynn, then,” she’s saying.

The coast is already aflame when they arrive - there is screaming, yes, but also the battlecries

“You have the stone?” someone asks abruptly.

“Whoa, lady,” Rocket snaps, and Jolie whips around to face a beautiful, brawny, blond-haired

“My name is Hildegarde, and I am a trusted friend of the true Allfather and an ally to Thor,”

Pete holds up a cautionary hand to the rest of them. “One of our party does.”

Hildegarde nods with a grim smirk. “I see you’re on guard against Loki masquerading as

Hildegarde looks out at the carnage with furrowed brows. “Thor said you are headed back to

“I’m gonna kill Drax,” Jolie can hear Pete muttering in the background. “I’m gonna kill
him.”
Hildegarde takes off, lunging into the fray of bullets and blasts and blood, shouting to Thor.
Thunder sounds, electricity crackles, and the golden god soars into the air, pulling the firing
blasts in his direction as he goes. He slams Mjolnir into the base of one of the Sakaaran
warship carriers, and the entire thing flips in the air a few times, the hull visibly crumpled.

“Now!” Hildegarde reappears just up the bridge, gesturing to them. Gamora’s drawn her

“Let’s go,” Rocket says, and leaps nimbly up on top of Groot’s shoulder.

They hit the bridge running, taking out any Sakaaran soldier that disembarks, shooting at the
battleships and war-pods and aiming for the engine vents when they get the chance.
Hildegarde and Gamora handle any short-range enemies with ease, but the crystalline bridge

“You good, doll?” she hears Rocket call, but she’s too focused to respond. The Gemma Lynn
is so close - so very close. As a group, they bank sharply around the side, toward the airlock,

Before them - previously hidden from view - is Drax on his knees, and Ronan looming above
him.

“I doubt I’ll remember killing you either,” Ronan is telling him, raising his cosmi-rod.

Jolie doesn’t think. If she had, she might’ve actually shot the Kree Accuser with her
quadblaster.

Instead - stupidly - she chucks her overheated laser pistol at him as hard as she can.

It clonks him solidly in the head.

Ronan wheels toward them as Jolie skitters backward, and he’s slamming down the hammer
in their general direction before she can even register it. The concussive force throws them all
back: even the muscle-bound Hildegarde crashes onto her shoulderblades and slides along the
bridge.

But Jolie is the closest, and when the wave of power hits her, she flies backward, lungs
emptying in mid-air, and something crunches in her leg. By the time she hits the ground, it

is all wrong: the thin stretchy fabric of her pants is torn and dark and sticky, and something

A moment of clarity is all she needs, she supposes.

But then Rocket’s there, trying to yank her up by her elbow, claws burying themselves deep

And Rocket is still in the way.

There’s a crackle of thunder, the ozone-like scent of electricity and fire, and a soft boom, and

“Let go, sweetheart. Frickin’ let go.”

It takes all her concentration to uncurl her fingers from where they’re locked around the

“Sorry sorry sorry sorry - ”

She hears the chanting before she realizes it’s coming from her own mouth - but she does

“I am Groot.”

“The Luphomoid cyborg - she got the stone while I was fighting Ronan,” she hears someone

“I. AM. GROOT.”

Then Pete’s moving past them - a blur, an impression of fury and intention - and Rocket is

“Sorry sorry sorry,” she’s still panting. “Sorry, that was so fucking stupid - I know, I’m a

She doesn’t feel the Gemma Lynn take off but she’s pretty sure they’re moving now. That, or

“Shut up,” Rocket’s spitting, furious. “I’m fine.” She thinks he’s demanding med packs. Drax
is subdued, handing them over. “Get this on Gamora,” she hears Rocket tells Groot. Her

Flora Colossus and thumping himself on the left side of his chest. “Right here,” Rocket says,

“He did,” Drax says solemnly from where he’s tucked himself, inconsolable against the

She thinks Rocket flinches, but it’s hard to be sure of anything right now. Her brain feels like

“It’s fine,” Jolie says, and she’s not even sure what she’s saying anymore. She thinks she

Rocket’s cursing again, and he snarls at Drax over his shoulder, “Get over here, tough guy.”

His face is grim. “This is gonna hurt. A lot. And this selfish, moronic shitbag -” he jabs a

Jolie feels her eyes go huge: a little burst of resistance behind all the exhaustion and hurting.

“You’re already on thin fuckin’ ice,” he snarls, softness forgotten, “so don’t argue with me.”
He gestures furiously to Drax, who obediently crouches on the floor behind her, takes her

Rocket looks down at her a moment, almost searchingly, and then winces at whatever he sees
in her face. “M’sorry, princess,” he mumbles, and snaps the med pack over her shattered shin.

The world is all blinding white-fire pain, clean and scalding, shot through with hot electricity:
exploding, collapsing, exploding again. She loses part of herself in the void for a moment,
and then almost as quickly as it flares, the screaming white fades.

Dissipates.

Dissolves.
Slowly, slowly, the world takes shape around her. She is aware that she has a mouthful of
coins, and her tongue is coated in the flavor of pennies and nickels. When logic sweeps in,
just enough to tell her it’s blood, she thinks it’s her own at first - but then some distant part of

“Water,” she hears Rocket snap at someone, and then Groot is pressing a cool mug into her

“No,” Rocket translates. “We just left Asgardian airspace. Quill’s got us on a circuitous route

were goin’.” Rocket’s pointing at Gamora, then at Jolie, but his eyes never leave Drax. “You

“I don’t - “ Jolie starts, and Rocket’s smashing her words out of the air with another sweep of

Jolie’s tired, and achy, but something in his words still open that crooked space behind her

“I am Groot.”

Rocket’s eyes go huge, then narrow.

“I said no.”

“If Ronan has the stone, he’s going to use it to wipe them out,” Gamora tells the room tiredly.

She hesitates. “Did Quill agree to abandon them?” she demands.
  Rocket flinches. “Quill agreed to focus on getting away until we could make a decision
  together,” he admits. “But come on. We’re one frickin’ ship and a small assortment of

Chapter Summary



      in which Xandar is saved and good lives are lost.



Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes



   It’s about 6 hours before they can reach Xandar, still following Quill’s 50-jumps-every-
   twenty-minutes plan. Four rotations would’ve been better on their bodies - this is too many
   jumps, without really leaving enough time to recuperate. Of course, if all this were just a
   frickin’ joy-ride, they could’ve taken a full two cycles each way.

   But the ride is remarkably low on any so-called joy, and unfortunately, speed is the only
   priority right now.

   And by speed, Rocket assumes everyone means hurtling toward their deaths.

   Jolie’s limping, shin and calf still mottled with wildflower-bruises. There’ll be a scar like a
   pink ribbon over the skin there once the contusions fade, but the medpack has done the most
   necessary work. Rocket knows she must still be feeling the swelling - the rub of muscle on
   bone, the ghost of fractures like a cobweb spidering across her tibia. She doesn’t sit though -
   of course she doesn’t, not till after she’s rationed out anti-inflammatories for everyone to help
   mitigate their inevitable jumpsickness.

   At least she’s grabbed some painkillers for herself and Gamora, though Rocket bets she only
   thought about it for the Zen-Whoberian’s sake. That concussive blast had taken her out too -
   maybe would’ve killed her. Busted ribs, and at least one had punctured a lung, probably from
   Quill trying to help her up. Then Groot had lifted Gamora to cradle her carefully onto the
   Gemma Lynn, and even with all his gentleness, Rocket’s pretty sure the big guy must’ve
   caused more soft-tissue damage. But what else could they do? At least they’d gotten the
   medpacks in time.

   And when had Rocket started caring so damn much, anyway? When had he started liking
   these idiots? When had he started thinking the Gemma Lynn only mattered as much as the
   morons onboard?

   Just in time for them all to end up dead, he broods.

   They all should eat but they’re too nervous. Employing his most-furious scowl, he makes Jo
   nibble on some dried fruit and orloni. To be honest, he’s gratified that it works - even if it’s
   just because she’s so fuckin’ soft that she hates to have him angry. Not that he isn’t already
   angry. But she’d lost a lot of blood, and he needs her to frickin’ eat.
She’d lost a lot of blood, and he needs her to eat.

Once she does so - narrowly avoiding him fully losing his fuckin’ mind at her - he huffs a
half-distracted good girl at her, and tries to just… sit. And listen. Jo, Gamora, and Quill are
all dreaming up some stupid plot, like if they can just put their wishes into words, things will
work out. Idiots and morons, each one of ‘em.

For possibly the first time, Rocket doesn’t have much to say. He’s just trying not to think
about how Jo had looked, spilled out on that crystalline Asgardian bridge, her hair slipping
out of her bun and her leg twisted at that sickening angle, one sharp spear of bone poking
through the torn legging above her boot.

He remembers what it’s like to have your bones busted open like that - broken up to be made
into something else. He’d been born into it. And he’s pretty sure he’d never have wanted that
kind of pain for her, not even when he’d thought he’d hated her. Thinking about it now makes
his stomach clench and revolt, trying to expel food that isn’t there.

And Drax said that piece-of-shit Ronan had stepped on her.

It’s almost the worst part of the whole thing. She’d been on some mindless crusade to - what?
Save them all? Save him, in particular, twisting him all up in her arms and underneath her
while being subjected to not just pain, but fuckin’ disrespect?

But it’s not the worst part - not quite.

The worst part is that for just a heartbeat or two, staring at Jo with a sickening hollowness in
his gut as she’d scrambled back and away from Ronan, he’d considered leaving her.

Even a cycle ago, even after he’d started thinking of her as some kind of friend - he’d have
left her in the dust if his or Groot’s life was on the line. He’s quick enough. Small enough.
He’s pretty sure he could’ve made it to the Gemma Lynn, if he’d tried. Left them all behind.

And what could he have done for her, anyway? How could he help her when he was only a
little more than half her height, disarmed by the concussive blast that had nearly thrown him
right off the bridge? What was he gonna do - be a crutch? There was no way she was getting
vertical with that kind of wound. But her gaze had found his like she’d been looking for it,
turning toward him like a fuckin’ flower wanting to face the sun. And her mouth had been
screwed up tight with pain, and her eyes had been so big in that pale, ashen face of hers.

She’d seen, he was sure. Even with her leg all crooked and wrenched, blood pouring
dangerously, she’d looked in his eyes and known he was thinking of abandoning her. And
what had she done? Not cursed him for a coward, even though she’d have been right to. No,
she’d looked at him with her stupid-soft eyes and the most apologetic twist to her lips.

Go.

And there, bright in his mind like a beacon, he’d remembered that moment between them:
less than two full rotations after he’d been his most bitter and mean-spirited, and barely one
day after she’d slept on the floor to keep his small-hearted, drunk ass company.
I think a lot about what I would’ve done if we hadn’t been able to get you off the Eclector,
she’d said.

What would you ‘a done?

Died trying.

Stupid. What does dying trying do? But he’d already known, because he’d fuckin’ felt it
when she’d first said it to him.

It lets a person know they haven’t been deserted.

So he’d leapt toward her - cursing her, cursing Drax, yelling for Groot - and he’d been
stupidly trying to get her up, to get her out of Ronan’s path. And her retaliation - the only

And he’d been stunned enough to let her. The whole galaxy had distilled into a panic of

That’s not true. He knows exactly when he last felt like that.

- sky -

Afterward, he’d learned from Groot that it had been Thor who’d saved them, blasting into

Because if any of these jackasses were being honest, they’d say it: it’s a shit plan. He opens

Like it’s supposed to be inspiring.

“Usually, life takes more than it gives,” the Terran man is saying. “But not today. Today, it’s

People deserve to have their memories.

She’s too frickin’ good at this. She’s too good.

For now, though, he just offers her the shower first. They have their own rooms, of course,
but - well, a few cycles ago, Rocket would have preferred to grieve alone, but if she’s already
here, he supposes there’s really no reason for her to leave. He sets the potted twig on the end
table near the head of the bed. She comes out of the washroom, toweling off her hair. Her
cheeks are pink and gleaming from the hot water, and she’s wrapped in one of the two fluffy
robes that had been left on hooks on the door. If he’d been feeling anything other than hollow,
he knows he’d be wondering what’s underneath it.

But there’s no space inside him for that right now. Strange: how a person can be so fuckin’
empty and still not have room for anything else.

Either way, he really needs to get those water-showers finished on the Gemma Lynn. If there’s
even any Gemma Lynn left.

He winces, because maybe that dream is dead now too.

Then he goes to shower himself, and when he’s done, he shakes himself off and towel-dries
his fur as well as he can before realizing there’s some kind of warm-air blaster that shoots out
of the ceiling when he pushes a button. Well, that’s nice, and he’s gonna figure out how to
replicate that too. His fur is almost completely dry in moments. The robe is stupid-big on
him, but he’s not putting his gross, dirty clothes back on when he finally feels… clean.

As clean as he ever feels, anyway.

When he leaves the shower room, drained, Jo’s sitting at the top of the bed, tracing a finger
on the rim of the pot. She’s still in the robe, and she’s placed her glove and her rectangular
black glass - cracked at one corner but otherwise miraculously unscathed - on the little
endtable beside the planted stick. He pauses, and then slides the keyplate out of his filthy
jumpsuit pocket, and carefully places it next to her slender brick of useless tech and
memories.

She looks up, and then moves to the edge of the bed, and just opens her arms.

He kind of hates himself for it, but he goes to her, and lets her envelope him and press her
mouth to the top of his head.

She’s so soft and warm all around him, and underneath the fancy Xandaran soft-soap, she
still smells like curlflower tea.

++++

Jo keeps a couple changes of new clothes in the room the Nova Corps arranged for her, but
it’s a veneer of separation. Her hairbrush and her sleep-shirt and everything else she uses on a
daily basis are tucked into a little drawer in his bathroom or his wardrobe, and every night he
curls up under her hands and every morning he wakes up pressed tight against her.

But at every turn, his brain keeps tripping on the scattered memories of the people he’s lost.
Groot is like a ghost-step at the end of the staircase. Rocket keeps putting his foot down, only
to find there’s no floor where he expected it to be.

One way to keep his mind distracted - or maybe to do the opposite, maybe to obsess - is by
checking on Jo’s leg every day. The medpack knit the bone up nicely, and even the skin itself.
The bruises have shifted from indigos into evergreens, and they’re starting to yellow, which
seems like a good sign. The scar itself is as annoyingly pretty as the rest of her, Rocket
thinks: pale-pink and satiny, like a tattered ribbon wound halfway around her leg. It’s holding
together strong. He hates that she has it, though. He knows how scars are bought with pain,
and how easy it is for them to make you feel ugly.

Yeah, he doesn’t want any part of that for her.

The third day that he demands to see it, Jo rolls her eyes dramatically, teasingly, and tells him
her bone doesn’t even ache anymore. The torn muscle just feels a little overstressed - nothing
to worry about. I’m not even limping anymore. It’s not a big deal.

It’s a mistake on her part. She’s already sitting on the edge of the bed where he’s ordered her,
and he’s crouching at her feet, pressing the glossy seam of her skin with testing fingers -
checking the color, the bloodflow. And suddenly - unaccountably quickly - he’s speechless
with fury. He can taste the enamel crunching between his gritted teeth. Everything is dark
sparks and white noise.

“…Rocket?”

Slowly - dangerously - he turns his eyes up to hers.

“Maybe you forgot what happened right before you got this thing,” he says, and he knows his
voice is a rumbled threat. “But I frickin’ haven’t.”

She winces. “Rocket. I - “

“You basically threw yourself at Ronan’s frickin’ feet. Like a fuckin’ present.”

He can see her lips go pale before they’re trapped by her teeth.

“Well?”

“Well, what?” she whispers.

I might kill her myself, he thinks, and laughs - a sharp, harsh bark before he rises up to his
feet. The anger is good. Familiar. It fills up the vacuum inside. He sinks into it, breathes it in,
becomes it. “You - “

“The present was for you,” she says, her voice all strangled and desperate. “If I - if I threw
myself at Ronan’s feet like a present, it was for you. For the rest of them, too. I’m not going
to - I am not going to apologize for that.”

You said you weren’t gonna leave, he thinks. You said you weren’t goin’ anywhere. It’s a
hypocritical thought though, isn’t it? ‘Cause he’d almost done the same thing. He’d almost
done worse.

“It was stupid,” he growls instead. “It was frickin’ reckless. We coulda - and then - “

He breaks off, because he can feel it again: the tug on his jumpsuit straps, the softness of her
and the scent of her and that ragged scream into his fur, like her throat had been torn right up
the inside -

His heart stutters against his metal sternum, then drops. He reaches for the rage again, and
pulls it tighter around him.

“It was stupid,” he repeats. Seethes. His clawed finger comes out to point at her. “Don’t do it
again.”

Jo stares at him mutely, big-eyed, and he already knows what she’s thinking because
apparently that’s a thing that happens when you spend too many rotations falling asleep to the
lullaby of someone else’s breathing.

I can’t promise that, he thinks in a mimicky, high-pitched falsetto.
“I can’t promise that,” she says. Her lips are bloodless and bitten.

He clenches both fists in front of his face, elbows bent and forearms so tight with anger that
they’re shaking, like he could rip his way through the air between them and then pull her ribs
apart, bury some fuckin’ common sense under her heart or inside her lungs. A tattered roar
claws its way up out of his throat and grinds through his bared teeth.

“Rocket - “

One arm snaps out, clawed finger pointing again.

“And I can’t promise I won’t lock you up in the goddamn ship,” he snarls, and his volume
rises. “I will fuckin’ keep you there as long as I have to so you don’t have the chance to do
anything so fuckin’ stupid again.”

She’s silent, her eyes stuck on him, unblinking and - sad.

There are cracks in all his hollow spaces, though, and the wrath is already leaking out. He can
feel it. Everything aches. “Don’t test me,” he snaps, trying to clutch at the rage because it’s
safer, because it’s something. “‘Cause I will.” He laughs again, and the sound is harsh and
bitter. “Believe me, princess, it would take nothin’ to convince me to keep you trapped in my
bunk for a cycle or two. Nothin’.”

She’s still not saying anything, and the bitterness starts seeping out of him too.

“I will,” he repeats. “I will fuckin’ lock you up if I have to.” He pauses, lungs heaving. Of
course he won’t. “I will. Once we get a new ship.” And then he’s pinching the bridge of his
nose, brow furrowed, eyes wet. Again. “Jo.”

“I’m here,” she says quietly, like she always knows the frickin’ question he hasn’t asked.

“I can’t - “ He swallows. “You can’t.”

“I know,” she says.

His damp eyes flick across her face, searching her - for what, he isn’t sure. But then he drops
his gaze to her leg, and its pink-ribbon scar.

“You gotta look out for yourself, Jo. Nobody else is gonna do it.”

She’s quiet again, and when he hazards another glance at her face, that softness is written in
every feature.

“You did,” she reminds him, and her words are so gentle.

His whole body recoils.

“You can’t trust me with that,” he says immediately, before he can even think about it. She’s
already backing off, palms out.
“Okay,” she murmurs, her voice a little soothing balm. “Okay. I’m sorry.”

“I was gonna dump you,” he tells her, all teeth and locked-down panic. “I was gonna leave
you there.” He’s not even sure if he means Asgard, or Xandar, or Conjunction. Fuck, he’s
such a jackass. “I was gonna fuckin’ leave you.”

“Okay,” she repeats, and her shoulders go soft. Every joint of her goes soft: no sharp edges,
no angles for him to cut himself on. “It doesn’t matter, Rocket. It doesn’t matter. I would’ve -
“

“You gotta take care of yourself, Jo,” he repeats, and his voice is haggard.

Her lips press together.

“Come here?” she says quietly. “I’m sorry for rolling my eyes at you. I’m sorry for - for
making light of it all. I shouldn’t have.”

“Don’t do it, Jo,” he tells her, trying to get back some of the warning growl. He’s not talking
about her stupid little jokes, and he knows she knows it too. “Say you’re not gonna do it
again.”

She grimaces - pained. She looks so forlorn - distraught over his anger, but unwilling to back
down. Her words, when they come, are soft little birds.

“You’re too important to me. I can’t promise - “

“I’ll hold it against you,” he tells her. “If you ever do anything like that again - there’ll be a
frickin’ reckoning. You’re not ready for that kind of fight - not with me - “

She tilts her head, and leans back slowly. “Will it help you feel better?” She’s got big, gentle
eyes, and open palms. She twists her mouth to the side in that sad, lopsided smile he hates,
then bends her elbows and curls her hands into fists to match his. And for fuck’s sake, her
form is frickin’ miserable. But she’s looking at him over her knuckles with those stupid-soft
eyes, and something inside that hollow space inside him splinters. Anything else he could’ve
held inside himself drains out: right down through the soles of his feet, into the plush pile of
the Xandaran carpet.

“‘Cause if it helps you feel better,” she tells him, “we can fight.”

His voice falters somewhere behind his prosthetic clavicle. He wants to take both of her fists
in his hands like they’re pieces of ripe fruit, press her knuckles against his teeth, open her
fingers and lap his tongue across the wells of her palms. Curl her hands closed again and
press them like round stones against his ribcage, so he can feel his heart beat against her
knuckles.

I wouldn’t stand a fuckin’ chance, he thinks, and his shoulders slump. He steps forward
without meaning to, and his hands rise in front of him. He watches his dark, scarred fingers
circle her wrists from a distance - a thing he never would’ve done, if he’d been inside his
frickin’ body at all. But he can feel each butterfly-bone under her skin, and he remembers
again how angry he’d been that first night on the Gemma Lynn, staring at her vulnerable,
delicate hand as it dangled over the side of her bunk.

He tugs her fists back down into her lap.

“You’re gonna break your frickin’ wrists like that,” he only tells her, and the words scrape his
throat raw.

“Thank you for checking my scar,” she says quietly. “Thank you for looking out for me.”

“I mean it, princess,” he repeats. “Don’t do that again. ‘Cause I promise you won’t like the
outcome.”

++++

Empty threats, really.

Not that he’d been lying about barricading her in his frickin’ bunk, or that he isn’t perfectly
willing to do it, though in better times - even just a few moments before losing Groot - those
fantasies had looked very different.

Lying next to her that night, letting her wrap herself around him, it occurs to him that he’s
been telling himself he’d decide whether or not to keep her after getting this frickin’ power
stone off his ship, but he’s been fooling himself. He can see that now.

He’s such a fuckin’ moron.

The sunrise brings a need, now, to distract himself from both the loss of his best friend and
Jo’s reckless goddamn behavior. He tries to refocus on the one thing that hasn’t failed him
yet, and that isn’t dependent on anyone but him: building deadly fuckin’ weapons.
Specifically, he wants to make sure Jo has at least one new firearm as soon as possible, since
she’d lost her quadblaster and her laser pistol on Asgard.

He starts with a plain old electric blaster, but he’s tweaking some things on it - gonna make it
pack more of a punch. He’s planning on making her something better as soon as he can get
his hands on new things, but the only other guns he has to offer right now are an enormous
laser cannon and a bulky ion blaster, and he knows she’s not gonna carry either of them, no
matter how much he tries to bully her into taking care of herself.

The souped-up electric blaster is still better than nothing. He wonders if he can convince Dey
to get him a Nova machine gun - the one he’d used briefly during their escape from the Kyln
had felt like pure power in his hands. He could use some of the parts to ramp up the blaster
even more, and still have plenty of new pieces left over to further enhance both his other two
firearms.

Dey is less than obliging, unfortunately. Rocket tries to figure out if he can get his hands on
one some other way.

Rotations pass. Then, a cycle. The newly-minted Guardians eat meals together, sometimes
with Corpsman Dey and his family, though it feels weird to Rocket. He waters his twig and
checks its soil religiously. In the evenings, Jo sometimes lures him out to the city, where the
Asgardians are currently celebrating with the Xandarans after each long day of rebuilding.
Thor buys him a lot of drinks. Sometimes the two of them sit while Jo makes herself scarce,
and Thor’s maybe not the brightest star in the heavens, but Rocket likes him. Sometimes it
feels good and takes his mind off… everything. But it also feels dangerous these days. To
like. And in general, Rocket’s mostly just tired and sick with grief.

The minute he feels his ears and tail droop, though, Jo’s already at his side, asking him if they
can leave. And some part of him knows she’s doing it on purpose. Watching him. Reading
him.

“I had a family once,” he tells her at some point, in their shared darkened room back at the
lodge. It’s all he says. He can’t say anything else. She’s still and quiet and probably can’t see
him at all, so he sits with the words, testing them out on the shadows.

“I know,” she says at last, and the two words are a quiet blanket on his shoulders.

It takes a while, but the city’s rebuilding is nearly done, and the Nova Corps are ready to
wrap up business. The Guardians of the Galaxy are welcome to live in the city, they say, but
the idea of living on Xandar leaves Rocket feeling claustrophobic, for more reasons than one.
When Nova Prime requests one final meeting, they collect Drax and head to Nova Corps
headquarters, where Quill and Gamora are waiting with Corpsman Dey.

Thor falls into step with them on the way.

“Friends,” he greets them heartily, and Rocket feels something inside him go colder at the
man’s familiarity in a way he hasn’t felt before. “I apologize again for our tardiness during
the final battle, but we’ve worked hard to put the city back to rights. I want to thank you
again for everything you’ve sacrificed in protecting the galaxy. All in a day’s work, I
suppose.”

Rocket grimaces. Thor’s kind of an angelic idiot, but he’s not usually this tone-deaf. Jolie’s
eyeing the golden man suspiciously, but honestly, Rocket is too tired to care.

“Your gratitude is accepted, and you are very welcome,” Drax says, as they enter the central
chamber. Their friends and the Nova Corps leaders look up at their entrance.

“Thor,” Nova Prime greets him. “Thank you again for coming to our aid yesterday. We look
forward to our future alliance.”

“Hmm, yes,” Thor says firmly. “I, too, look forward to it. But in the meantime, I do wonder if
we made a poor judgment call in sending the power stone here in the first place. Perhaps it is
unfair of us to expect you to hold it, when such dangerous people will continue to pursue it.
You are not gods, after all, and it would be a tragic shame to see our new allies become a
target for those with nefarious purposes.”

“Thanos,” Gamora murmurs under her breath, and the god of thunder nods solemnly.
Nova Prime is hesitating, and it looks like she’s considering Thor’s offer. “We must prioritize
our people’s welfare,” she concedes. “Tell me - “

“What would you recommend, Thor?” Jolie interrupts, and now Rocket’s ears and eyes
sharpen anyway, because he recognizes that too-polite tone.

It sounds like the same tone she’d used on the crew of the Faraday.

“You had asked if I could suggest another keeper for the stone,” Thor tells her, and his voice
is perhaps too jovial, all things considered. “I had given it some thought on our way here, and
there is another Elder at the far reaches of the universe. He calls himself the Champion, and I
believe he has the means to protect the power stone from any who might mean to seize it for
themselves. We can make arrangements, and my Warriors Three will be happy to collect it
from you and deliver it under guard - “

“Okay,” Jolie says pleasantly, and now she’s standing in that familiar wide-legged stance,
brand new electric blaster already pulled and leveled squarely at Thor’s face, shirt falling off
one shoulder.

“Jolie!” Quill blurts out, aghast, and Nova Prime and Dey are both gasping, flustered and
half-panicked at the possibility of some kind of intergalactic incident. Gamora looks like
she’s got the beginnings of a migraine.

But to Rocket, it’s almost nostalgic - yeah, the Faraday. The way Jo had shoved the barrel of
her quadblaster in that guy’s mouth. He can’t help but feel an admiring little grin twitch the
corner of his lips.

And Jo’s ignoring them all, just smiling that one smile that shows all her teeth, and looking
directly into Thor’s eyes.

Still hot, Rocket thinks, and he supposes that might be a sign that he’s starting to climb his
way out of the hole in his chest.

“We just got our records expunged,” Quill’s pleading, but Jo doesn’t even spare him a glance,
keeping her eyes and smile locked on the golden god.

“What…are you doing, Lady Jolie?” Thor asks, as if he’s flabbergasted.

She only smiles sweetly up at him, her voice saccharine. “Fuck around and find out, buddy.”

Yeah. Still hot.

There’s a long moment of silence, and then the god sighs heavily. He exhales slowly,
shoulders dropping - and somehow, slowly, they keep deflating, until the other, slimmer,
darker Odinsson is standing there. “It was worth a shot,” Loki says mildly. He shrugs at Jo
with a lofty little curl to his lip, and then - vanishes.

Jolie holsters her weapon and turns back to the rest of them. “What?” she says blankly, as if
she’s just noticed the Nova Corps members and certain elements of her own crewstaring at
her. Drax alone seems completely unaffected by the whole scenario, but Rocket is never sure
when the big guy is completely with them.

Rocket looks at her - looking around - and snickers in spite of himself. The sound crackles in
the silent chamber. It’s like the release of a pressure valve on his lungs, and for just a second,
his shoulders ease.

“Well,” says Dey. “Uhm. Glad you caught that - “

“Thor mentioned the other night that he was planning to leave soon for Terra, to look for his
father. I wasn’t sure if he’d left yet, but… “ Jolie shrugs, and makes her little humming noise.
“I’m sure he’d want me to give you all his regards. He did say the other Asgardians will stay
as long as they’re wanted for help with rebuilding, and that Asgard is, uhm, honored to be
Xandar’s ally from this day forward.”

Nova Prime clears her throat. “Well,” she says, “thank you - for, ah, relaying the message.
And on behalf of the Nova Corps, we'd like to express our profound gratitude for your help in
saving Xandar, as well.” She offers a small, close-lipped smile. “If you would be so kind as
to follow Denarian Dey, he has something to show you.”

“Wow, uh…thank you, Nova Prime,” Quill says.

“Thank you,” Gamora adds, and Jolie dips her head.

Rocket just shrugs internally, and resettles the pot in his arms.

They follow Corpsman Dey, stepping out onto the rooftop landing pad. There, gleaming in
the bright Xandaran sun, is a ship.

It’s a massive ship, way bigger than the Gemma Lynn - but there are massive stretches of it
that look like they came from her.

Quill gasps, and Jo lets out a strangled little sound.

“We tried to keep them both as close to the originals as possible.The Milano was brought out
of impound, and we salvaged as much of the Gemma Lynn as we could. But…we thought
you might like some upgrades. Both ships can operate as normal, independent of each other,
but there’s a docking port that allows the Milano to fully integrate as an extension of the
Gemma Lynn. When functionally docked, the Gemma Lynn’s controls will act as primary.”

Jo says nothing. Her eyes are doing that shimmery thing.

Even Quill’s speechless - well, as much as he ever is. “Wow. I…thank you.”

Rocket has a brief urge to snark something like, yeah, thanks for fixing up my ship without
asking, but that’s a lot of energy right now, and he kinda hopes they added some frickin’
showers. And Jo looks so soft and happy, for just a moment.

He’s not sure he’s seen her like that in rotations. Maybe once or twice on the way to Asgard.
Otherwise, not since before the Kyln.
He thinks again - about her red blood over shifting opal glass. Of her mouth in his fur,
screaming. He hasn’t thought of it in a rotation or two, which he supposes is progress.
Nevertheless, he has to pummel down the shudder that races his spine, trying to escape
through his shoulders.

Dey casts a solemn eye on each of them. “I have a family - and they’re alive because of you.”
He clears his throat, like he maybe got choked up for a minute. “As Quill mentioned inside,
those of you with criminal records have had them expunged. However, I do have to warn you
all against breaking any laws in the future.”

Rocket’s ears twitch and now he can’t hold back. “Question,” he proposes. “What if I see
something that I want to take, and it belongs to someone else?”

Dey blinks. “Well. You’d be arrested.”

Rocket blinks right back at him. “But what if I want it more than the person who has it?”

Dey looks at Jo, confused and almost like he expects her to translate. Rocket can feel himself
scowl.

“Hey, Dey. Buddy. Eyes down here. I’m the one askin’ the frickin’ question.”

“Uhm, that would still be illegal.”

Rocket shakes his head, grimacing. “That doesn't follow. No, I want it more, Dey. Do you
understand?”

Gamora chuckles from behind him, and even Jo looks like she’s barely holding back a
snicker.

“What are you both laughing at? Huh? I can't have a discussion with this gentleman?”

Drax steps up behind him. “What if someone does something irksome and I decide to remove
his spine?”

Dey shakes his head. “That's...that's actually murder. It's one of the worst crimes of all.” He
looks at Jo, at Quill, at Gamora. “So…also illegal.”

The Kylosian grunts, and then moves toward the ship, and Rocket waits, gripping his potted
twig.

“They’re gonna be fine, Dey,” Quill says. “I’ll keep an eye on them.”

“We’ll keep an eye on each other,” Jo corrects with a raised eyebrow, and Quill offers up a
guilty little smile and shrugs. “Wanna go home?” she asks, and casts her eyes to Rocket.

Do you want to come home?

Let’s go together.
  He nods, and steps toward her so they can stride up the ramp together. He clears his throat as
  they board. “So, uh, who’s gonna fly this thing?”

  “You and I,” Jolie says immediately.

  “Hey now,” Quill interrupts, jogging a few steps to keep up with them. “I’m also bringing a
  ship to this rig - arguably the better, sleeker, quicker ship. So I’m pretty sure I’m the captain
  now.”

  “Oh, are you?” Jo asks, grinning.

  “I am,” Quill says firmly. “And we’re gonna have to have a name for it when it’s docked
  together.”

  “Not one you pick,” Jo returns, her tone even.

  Then she laughs, and it’s a good sound.

  And for a moment, Rocket thinks maybe things can be okay after all.

  If he lets it be.

    Chapter XII. So Much It Hurts.

                                   Chapter 12: So Much It Hurts.
Chapter Summary



      in which we try not to fuck up the vibes.



Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes



   It takes some time to adapt to the new ship. The first day, Rocket refuses to go anywhere
   outside of Xandar’s vicinity until they find a market where he can get a Honchi Everbloom to
   keep in the console.

   Jolie’d had one on the Gemma Lynn for the last five years or so - a little trinket she’d picked
   up once on impulse, just dried petals frozen in a kind of amber. She’d been told in a
   marketplace that everbloom amulets were supposed to protect against collisions in jump-
   points: a charming bit of intergalactic superstition that she’d felt like indulging in a moment
   of whimsy. When the ship is broken down as it enters the jump and reconstituted on exit, the
   Everbloom supposedly keeps all the bits of quantum information exactly where it's supposed
   to be. Nothing gets lost, and nothings gets mixed with other passing ships. Jolie had actually
   forgotten the Everbloom was there - hadn’t thought it was important to Rocket, not when
   they have info-coating and a UNTN-capable drivetrain to do the heavy lifting of jump-point
   navigation - but here he is, lugging around his potted Groot and demanding they scour
   neighboring planets before they even think about hitting a jump. It takes four rotations to find
   one, and Rocket tucks the everbloom amulet into a little crevice in the dashboard, almost
   reverently.

   Within the first cycle, Quill moves back into his quarters in the Milano. Gamora and Drax
   seem more hesitant to relocate, perhaps just because they’ve gotten used to the Gemma Lynn
   since escaping the Kyln. Jolie’s grateful, honestly, because Drax still being in her old bunk
   gives her an excuse - however flimsy - to continue sleeping in Rocket’s bed.

   If Rocket notices that there are now two open bunks between the partnered ships that she
   could choose from, he doesn’t say anything. Each night, he places the pot - with its bit of
   Groot - on the desk next to the bed. He returns to his old nighttime routine of beginning the
   sleep shift in his hammock, only climbing onto the shelf-bed with Jolie after she’s fallen
   asleep - as if they hadn’t spent more than two full cycles sharing a Xandaran lodging room
   with only a single bed.

   She doesn’t acknowledge the return to old habits, but a few times he accidentally wakes her -
   and when she sleepily strokes the fur on his head or back, he doesn’t flinch at all.
There had been one night when she’d woken deep in the sleep rotation, and Rocket had been
nowhere to be found. She’d gone looking for him - just her white button down and her messy
bun and the pair of flimsy boots she’d pulled on to protect her feet from the grated floors.
The soft soles of her boots had whispered against the grates, and the velvet-blue corridors had
been rich with shadows. She’d finally found him in one of the cargo holds - the one which
Groot had occasionally used as a retreat - and she immediately wondered why she had taken
so long to look there.

He’d been sitting on the floor in the dark, next to his potted twig, with a datapad on the floor
in front of him. The tiny projector had filtered a small holovid into the dark: a miniature
version of Groot, captured in silvery light - an accidental recording that had never been
intentionally created, much less kept. How the recording had even made it into storage will
remain forever a mystery, but Jolie had been immediately glossy-eyed with gratitude that it
had.
