Pete shakes his head. “To borrow your own turn of phrase, Earthgirl - not telling him? That’s
fucked.” He hesitates. “I think he’d wanna know.”

She huffs out another grim little chuckle. “I think he’d run.”

“Does he…know anything? About you? How you ended up out here and…everything?”

She’s already shaking her head. “I promised I would tell him. Like, right after we left
Knowhere. But…I don’t know. Like I said, I’m not trying to fuck up the vibe.” She chews her
lip.

“I don’t…it’s not fucking up the vibe, Jolie. It’s…” Pete trails off, then says tentatively, “I’m
just saying that now seems like as good a time as any. Especially since you love him. Things
are good now. Things are calm. We’re all safe.” He hesitates. “You could.”

She breathes in heavily. Maybe he’s right. But Rocket’s already carrying such a weight, and
her own obnoxious story seems small in comparison, even though the telling of it will
probably have her a wreck for days.

She can’t afford that.

“I’ll take it under advisement,” she says as lightly as she can, and walks in front of him to
check and make sure everything is evenly trimmed. She hums, pulling gently on a few
handfuls of closely-cut hair to make sure there are no long strands hiding on his scalp, and
changes the subject. “So. As you were saying. About you and Gamora?”

He shrugs a little, shifting his head right as she’s touching up a spot, and she swats his
shoulder.

“I said, don’t move when I’m cutting!”

“Sorry,” he repeats sheepishly. “I mean, we kind of have…something. I think. We’re getting
there. It’s like…an understanding.”
She snorts and circles him for one last check, then turns off the redrazor. “Then why the hell
were you giving me shit about Rocket?”

He pauses, seeming to really consider her question. “I just wanted to make sure you were
happy,” he says after a moment. “And I don’t want you hurting. It’s important to me.”

She softens, dusts the stray golden hairs off the top of his head and shoulders, and drops a
kiss on his crown. “Your happiness is important to me, too, Brother-of-Mine.”

She rests her chin atop his head.

“Now. Broom’s in the utility closet. Sweep up this hair, Star-Lord.”

++++

Groot is definitely growing now. He has blinking black eyes and a sweet little mouth, and the
softest brush of green sprouts on top of his head. He has two little branch-arms, with tendril-
like fingers blooming at the ends. All day, he’s teasing and playing games with the rest of
their family: dancing, freezing, charming them with silliness.

In particular, he loves to dance - but he won’t around Drax. At first, Jolie thinks it’s just
another of Groot’s games - but sometimes she worries that he’s picked up on Drax’s opinion
of dancing. She can already tell Drax will be utterly charmed by anything their family’s baby
does, but the person who needs to know that most is Groot.

At night, when Rocket brings the Flora Colossus down to the bunk, Groot makes soft little
rumbles - groot…groot; groot - and Rocket watches him quietly with his heart in his eyes,
and Jolie watches them both like the moment is made of the thinnest planes of etched glass.
She wonders if Rocket knows how transparent he is in these unguarded moments.

She decides he doesn’t, and that she is extraordinarily blessed to bear witness to them.

She also tries to clean up her language. She has a few too many f-bombs in her vocabulary to
be throwing around in front of the little guy.

And yeah, she’s in love. She’s in love with this massive hodge-podge family they’ve made,
she’s in love with this new adopted son of theirs, she’s in love with her copilot. And if Rocket
feels all his love tinged with anger and fear, then she feels hers tinged with sadness and loss.
She’s full-up of love, and it’s all bittersweet.

On Martzi, they have a couple days of quiet, and Rocket brings Jolie a disk the size of her
palm. He hands it to her casually, but she can feel the excitement radiating off him,
resonating on her skin.

He’s perfected the Aero-Rig.

“You figured out the pocket dimension tech already?” she asks with a grin. She supposes she
should feel incredulous, but she doesn’t. He’s too clever for it to have been any kind of actual
challenge, even with all the other stuff he’s been making at the same time.
He scoffs. “Kid stuff,” he tells her, and winks - the expression is so exaggerated, so
ridiculous, that she can’t help but laugh out loud. “Wanna try this thing with me, princess?”

“Fuck yes,” she says, embracing the curse since Groot’s not around. “You’ve already made
me wait so long.”

Something heated flickers in Rocket’s eyes at that, but he just tsks - “Language” - before
jumping up to slap the little disk against her back. The blow is hard enough to make her
stumble - which she’s sure is intentional - and she shoots him a playful scowl. The armor
snaps out, clipping over the top half of her torso, and then she wiggles a little. The folds of
her too-large sweatshirt bunch up in places, and she tugs on the soft fabric till she’s
comfortable.

He shows her how to work it, what to press, how to maneuver.

“Keep your core tight and your back straight,” he instructs, “or you’ll be flopping all over the
place.”

“You sure I’m not gonna fall out of the sky?” she challenges with a crooked, teasing smile.

“You scared, sweetheart?” he throws back, and she laughs.

The rig jolts her a little when it first fires up. She wobbles a little but follows his instructions,
and the ascent settles into smoothness. Then they’re gliding, racing, and Rocket’s cackling,
and she’s laughing with him. When they land, they’re both breathless, and for just a while,
the weight Rocket’s always carrying seems lighter.

“So are you going to tell me about pocket-dimension tech yet?” she asks, trying to wriggle
out of the Aero-Rig so she can collapse it. She reaches behind herself for the disk between
her shoulderblades - over her shoulder, then up behind her back. No luck. It’s placed in a spot
just too far difficult for her to really tap it with enough force to get it to release. Fuck, she
thinks, and wriggles again before looking at him pleadingly. “Can you help me get this off,
please?”

He glances over at her - and freezes, eyes wide and jaw just a little ajar. His gazes skates her
from ankles to the knot of hair at the top of her head, before his mouth snaps shut and his
eyelids drop to half-mast. Slowly, he crosses his arms over his chest, then leans back casually
against the hull of the Gemma Lynn like he’s content to watch her struggle.

“I’m sure you can reach it, princess,” he says, and his voice is lower than she’s used to. It
always surprises her when he does that, because she never remembers it’s possible for him to
just drop an octave - his voice is already so deep. Gravelly. The rumble of it scrapes over her
nerves. “Try a little harder.”

She makes a face at him, then reaches up behind herself again, back arching. He stares at her
through half-lidded eyes for a moment as she squirms. “I really can’t, Rocket.” He doesn’t
move, and for a second, she wonders if she’s actually going to have to find Quill or Gamora
to help her get out of the thing. “Please? Rocket?”
He makes a weird sort of noise in the back of his throat, but before she can say another word,
he’s skirting behind her. “Helpless,” he mutters, tapping the disk between her shoulderblades
- more gently this time, she notices. The armor clinks back into its pocket dimension,
disappearing inside itself.

She scoffs, but the sound is light and she keeps her voice delicate and playful. “You’re telling
me you can’t design something that I can reach? I thought you were a mechanical and
engineering genius or something.”

He narrows his eyes. “Better watch it. Next time I’ll leave you tangled up. Just watch you try
to get loose.”

It’s such a weird choice of words that her brain trips over it for a second, then moves on. She
snorts. “No, you won’t.”

He raises a brow. “No? That some kind of dare?”

Never mind that for a moment she’d been worried he was going to do exactly that. She
bumps his shoulder lightly with her hip. “Nope. You like me too much.”

He blinks up at her, then looks away, rolling the two disks in his hands and muttering
something about making them more accessible.

“So,” she prods playfully. “Pocket dimension tech?”

He snorts then, back to his normal self - whatever that is. “I told you, I’m not trying to put
you to sleep with shit you don’t understand right now. And -” he adds sharply, clawed index
finger raised in warning “- no wearing your hair down with these things. Best case scenario,
you incinerate the ends, and then I have to smell your burnt hair all night. Worst case, you’ll
get stuck or screw something up and end up crashing back to ground.”

“Yes sir,” she teases, but she takes his point. “Whatever you say.”

They bicker their way back onto the Gemma Lynn/Milano, but every bit of it is good-natured
and light and fuck, she is happy. She can’t remember the last time she felt so content.

Unfortunately, it doesn’t take long for that weight to come back over him - and, if she’s being
honest, for her own reality to sink back onto her shoulders, too. Her smile grows soft and she
can feel a kind of wistfulness creeping in like ivy and wisteria. Without thinking, she strokes
her thumb over the fur behind one of his ears, just once - snatching her fingers back as soon
as she realizes what she’s doing. His ears twitch, but it’s the only indication that he’s even
noticed.

Now is as good a time as any, Quill had said.

Yeah, right. Not a fucking chance.

Chapter Summary



      in which a lost sister is found and Drax grapples with the concept of sarcasm.

   It’s cycles on cycles of relative peace. Rocket spends his time picking over any weaponry he
   can find on any planet they land on. He gets the water-showers up and running: three pods,
   plus hot clean water practically in perpetuity thanks to his newly-rigged rapid-refiltration and
   heating system. Next upgrade will probably be that air-dryer he remembers from Xandar.
   Water-showers are the best, but trying to get dry has its challenges when a person’s covered
   in fur.

   Jo helps - well, sort of. She knows some basics - whatever she’s needed to learn to keep the
   Gemma Lynn functional, he imagines. At least, as long as he pretends to forget that frickin'
   nightmare with the hexapull and the engine room door. But mostly, he’s having her hold shit,
   hand him tools, and manage the more straightforward tasks. He talks her through some of the
   more complicated stuff he’s doing but frankly, sometimes he relies too much on intuition to
   know how to explain it. In those moments, he kind of wishes he was a better teacher, which is
   a thought he’s never had before in his life.

   To be honest, trying to work with Jo means that each project takes longer than if he’d done it
   himself. But the truth is - and he still hates to admit it, even to himself - he’s come to like her
   company. Kind of crave it, sometimes, if he’s being honest. Her softness and warmth, just
   next to him. She touches him far more liberally than he would’ve ever imagined another
   person willingly doing - not unless he’d paid them, not unless it was to hurt him - and far
   more often than he would’ve imagined himself allowing.

   That said, he knows he’s returning the favor discreetly, a hundred times over. Leaning over
   her shoulder to adjust her hold on a laser-drill that she’s gripping perfectly fine on her own,
   tucking his nose under the curve of her jaw while he checks her aim, tapping the inside of her
   knee with one paw to widen a stance that really only needs to be widened for, uh,
   aestheticalistic purposes.

   Sharing the Aero-Rigs with her had been frickin’ exhilarating. And the way she’d looked
   after - pink-cheeked, wind-blown, eyes all glossy, twisting herself up into a pretty little
   package while she tried to reach the disk on her back - it had almost given him a frickin’
   hard-on right there, out of nowhere. He’d looked at her and all he could think about was how
   candy-sweet she was, and how much he wanted to get his mouth on her clit.
It would take nothin’ to convince me to keep you trapped in my bunk for a cycle or two.

In retrospect, he knows it was because of the adrenaline and endorphins from, you know,
fucking flying. Of course - he can admit to himself now that he’s attracted to her. Of course -
who wouldn’t be? But that near-lapse in judgment and self-control had only been the
reasonable result of sleeping together for cycles now, and then getting buzzed on flight.

That was it.

He definitely does not take any liberties when he wakes up next to her and her shirt has
ridden up, or she’s pulled him into her chest, or he finds them in some other frickin’...
situation. Yeah, he hasn’t taken advantage.

But he also hasn’t taken any steps to prevent it.

Can I touch you?

If he asked, it wouldn’t be about adjusting her fuckin’ aim. But he won’t. Because in his
fantasies, she always says yes, in that sweet, breathy way of hers -

And if he asks her, for real - well, he can’t imagine the answer will be the same. And that
might frickin’ kill him.

Not that he deserves anything else.

On top of that, she’s started noticing when he’s having a bad day, physically-speaking. Or
maybe she’s always noticed, and he’s just noticing her noticing now. It wouldn’t surprise him
- he remembers the way she’d looked at his glass cutter, the way she’d quietly assessed all the
modifications he’s made to his tools so he can still use them when the metal and bones and
tendons in his hands start aching. But now he sees her clocking it - no matter how hard he
tries to hide it - when he’s got a hitch in his step or tension in his shoulders.

Nobody else seems to notice. But she’s… she’s looking. And she’s too damn good at seeing.

And then, one night, she asks him, her voice tentative and small while Groot snores on his
little shelf:

Can I touch you?

Trust frickin’ Jo to ask first, and for it to mean nothing he’d been fantasizing about.

“It’s a Terran human thing,” she tells him with a shrug. “We’re evolutionarily predisposed to
crave contact. Babies will die if they don’t get enough physical affection.” She gives him that
sunshine-smile, like she thinks it’s gonna win him over. “You’d be doing me a favor.”

He stares at her, deadpan, because he can see right through her these days - she’s so frickin’
stupid-sweet it hurts sometimes - and frankly, she’s fuckin’ predictable. But when he opens
his mouth to tell her that, what comes out instead is a hoarse okay, and when she asks him to
lay on his stomach next to her, he does it without protest.
‘Cause he’d love to be the one ordering Jo around in bed, but he fuckin’ knows who’s really
in charge between them, knows he’ll take whatever she’ll give him.

And give she does. At first he freezes up under her hands, teeth gritted, old anger rising. He
hates that she’s touching all his scars, the gnarled flesh where his fur can’t grow: ugly and
coarse. He knows she probably can’t see much of him in the dark but he feels like she can,
feels like the creepiest little monster to ever crawl out of a cage and dare to look at the stars.

But her fingers are patient and coaxing and gentle. They find the spots where his muscles
have been contorted, where they’re seizing up in misdirected retaliation for the abuses
they’ve suffered. She traces silken patterns through his fur and over his damaged flesh, light
as raindrops or snowflakes. Her thumbs and knuckles ease deep into knots, luring them out of
hiding. Over and around the larger planes of muscle, he feels her palms: firm, kneading,
gliding.

At some point, he vaguely realizes he’s become soup. Every bone and metal plate in his body
feels like it’s melted inside him like so many ceremonial candles of Indigarran beeswax. The
pain will maybe always be there, but it’s a hundred jump-points away right now, just the
barest flicker of a distant sun buried deep in space and time.

“Thank you,” she murmurs at some point, her breath close enough that his ear flickers
instinctively. “For letting me.”

It’s fuckin’ ludicrous, is what it is. Her little whispered gratitudes, when she’s the one so
obviously making his miserable life better.

It makes the line he’s toeing a lot harder to stay clear of. A guy could get drunk off a girl like
this, a girl touching him like this. Then thanking him for it.

He barely finishes the thought before he’s asleep, and when he wakes in the morning, his
body feels looser and lighter than it has in - well, since as far back as he can remember. And
she acts like she doesn’t even notice, like she hasn’t just changed his frickin’ life with a few
well-placed knuckles.

But so far - so far - he’s managed to hold himself in check, to not wriggle himself inside her
stupid sleepshirt and try to live there. Not just for his sake and hers, but also because Groot is
always there - a quiet little presence on the workbench or in the kitchenette. It’s bad enough
that the kid is being raised by this screwed-up, weird little murder-club. At least, Rocket
thinks, the little guy is surrounded by people who will look out for him, and who love him.

The kid is developing at a solid pace - not that Rocket really knows how a Flora Colossus is
supposed to develop. But everything seems good. Groot’s ability to communicate - if not his
physical ability to speak - is growing every day and he’s developing a kinda smart-ass
attitude, but…he’s the son of Rocket’s best, closest, longest friend, the Groot who sacrificed
himself for everyone, and Rocket can’t bring himself to curb it.

Besides, Rocket has an attitude himself, and it’s served him well enough over the years.

Mostly.
When Rocket wakes up one morning and finds Groot’s pot empty of everything but Jolie’s
potting soil, he almost loses his mind with panic. He’s shouting Groot’s name before he
thinks better of it, and Jo jerks upright in the shelf-bed and lunges so far that she falls right
off it. Rocket would have probably started laughing his ass off if he hadn’t been so frantic to
find his adopted son.

Then the little guy toddles out from a honeycomb shelf he’s somehow climbed into, and the
relief hits so hard that Rocket’s bones ache.

Other than that moment of blind terror, everything has been… nice. And comfortable. Which,
paradoxically, is supremely uncomfortable. Sometimes Rocket looks at the line of Jo’s neck,
framed by whatever shining streamers have fallen out of the messy knot on top of her head,
and something inside him itches and builds. Or he looks around the common area, at all these
idiots taking jabs at each other, and he feels a twinge in his chest cavity that’s new. Once or
twice, he’s thought - is this what it feels like to be happy? - and then immediately realized,
no, it’s the threat of being happy.

Those days, he’s always a little meaner than he intends to be.

It’s these moments that make him realize that his apprehension is growing daily, rising like a
tidal wave on Morag, and sooner or later it’s going to drown him. The push-and-pull of
wanting desperately to be with his adopted son, to be with Jo, to be with all of these morons -
and the knowledge that they’re only going to end up hurt, probably because of his own
carelessness - is enough to give him new nightmares all over again.

“So, where to tomorrow?” Quill is asking. Gamora has pulled up the comms and is running
through a series of transmissions to check for distress calls, or other possible jobs.

Rocket’s tucked himself into a corner of the couch, and he’s working on yet another

He fixes a practiced expression of nonchalance on his face. “What was that about, anyway?”

“Gamora found out that her sister has been apprehended by the Sovereign authorities,” Drax
informs him solemnly. “They are willing to trade the Luphomoid in exchange for guarding
their harbulary batteries - “

Rocket blinks, concentration broken, and stares at Drax like the idiot he is. “Okay, first of all,
I got that,” he interrupts. “Second of all, it ain’t harbulary, moron. It’s anulax.”

“That is what I said. Harbulary.”

Rocket closes his eyes and shakes his head. “Unbelievable.”

When he opens his eyes and hazards a glance in Jo’s direction, she’s already facing the
screens again, rereading whatever the Sovereign listing says.

“Jo?”

She hums a distracted sort of acknowledgement, saves the transmission, and closes out the
screen with her back still to the room. Rocket feels his shoulders tense. He racks his brain,
but he can’t think of a time when she hasn’t immediately turned toward the sound of his
voice like a little Xandaran field-daisy searching for the sun.

Which is a stupid thought to have. Of course there must’ve been times when she hadn’t
responded.

Nope, some shitty little part of him argues. Not even when she’d had her leg busted open and
crushed in by that shitbag Ronan. She was still looking for you. Always.

“I am Groot?” asks Groot from the coffee table, and now she does turn.

Her eyes are exhausted. She looks like she’d been cut open and emptied, and then had to
refill herself by hand.

“Yeah,” Jo says. “I - “ She breaks off, then shrugs and smiles wanly - first at Groot, then at
Rocket. “Sorry. I’m fine.”

“You look like you’ve just aged a hundred years,” Rocket informs her skeptically.

She grimaces, then winks, but it’s half-hearted at best. “Charmer.”

“Turn on some of Quill’s tunes,” he suggests, but he’s watching her with narrow eyes. “You
gonna come back and work on this thing?” He gestures to her book with the loose laser
cannon barrel he’s holding.
“Mmhmm,” she murmurs, but she looks conflicted. She ducks away onto the bridge for a
moment, and then the quick, thoughtful strains of Landslide flutter over the sound system.
She weaves her way back between the couches, one hand flickering over Rocket’s shoulder in
a way that quells his rising tension - for a second. She sits back down at her vice and picks up
her brush.

And then…she just kind of sits there, adopting Drax’s middle-distance stare.

It’s about ten minutes of her not moving, and even Drax has noticed. The Kylosian is now
looking at her in concern, too.

“Is she unwell?” Drax utters in a ludicrously-loud whisper, speaking from the side of his
mouth toward Rocket.

“I am Groot?”

“She’s fine,” Rocket says, but his eyes are locked on Jo. All his old tension is back, full-
force. His fur is bristling at the edges, and he clears his throat. “You with us, doll?”

She looks up suddenly. “Hmm? Oh, yeah,” she agrees, and then frowns down at the book she
has clamped in her vice. “Uhm, I do think all this detail-work is giving me a headache
though. I might head to bed early.”

He’s staring straight at her now, his expression flat, because that’s a frickin’ lie. The first lie
he’s ever heard from her, he thinks. He feels like she’s just knocked the air right out of his
lungs. That familiar, defensive meanness in him rises, and he strangles it down.

She’s already packing up her things, and her hands are shaking a little.

“Good night, Drax,” she says, holding the vice and the book and all her little tools cradled
against her chest.

“The night will be average, and I do not expect more,” the Kylosian intones, and Rocket rolls
his eyes even as Jo’s mouth stutters out a half-smile.

“I’m wishing you a good night, then,” she corrects herself, and then bobs down and drops a
kiss on the top of Groot’s head. “You too, Sprout,” she murmurs, and the little Flora Colossus
reaches for her. She plucks him up in her one free hand and lets him nuzzle into her cheek
before returning him to the tabletop. “Rocket.” Her smile is strained at the edges, and that
free hand reaches out to brush over his shoulder again.

He does recoil, this time. He doesn’t even mean to, but instinct takes over, and he lurches out
of reach.

She looks like he slapped her.

He hasn’t felt regret this strong in a while. It isn’t like he’s forgotten what a jackass he can be,
but he’d let himself get lulled into some sort of complacency. He should do something. He
should say something.
But she’s gone, trying to clutch all her stuff in one arm while she descends the ladder, cursing
when she drops something and then calling up “Sorry!” because he knows she’s been trying
to curb her language lately. If he weren’t so distracted by her weird behavior and her fuckin’
lie, it would’ve made his mouth twitch in a grin.

“Don’t say shit like that,” he tells Groot seriously, and the little guy nods solemnly.

“I am Groot.”

“No! No, not like that either!”

++++

“You should not have stayed up here.”

Rocket blinks up from the rifle. He’d been torn when Jo had left - feeling like he should have
gone with her, should’ve apologized for pulling away like that, demanded to know why she
was acting so frickin’ weird. Something. But Groot is still wide awake, and she’d clearly
wanted to be alone - so much so that she’d lied to his frickin’ face. So he and Groot have
stayed on the upper level, and Rocket has been trying to distract himself by tinkering.

Until this big lug decided he had something to say.

“Huh?” Rocket asks eloquently. Drax is frowning at him.

“You should not have stayed up here.”

“What the hell are you talking about?”

“Jolie is distressed. You should go and be with her.”

“Why the hell would I do that?” Rocket asks, stomping down the part of himself that has
been saying the same thing.

Drax is staring down at him disapprovingly, and Rocket can feel his half-raised hackles
sliding higher.

“Because she needs someone to share in and ease her suffering,” the Kylosian says
reasonably, “and you are the best person to comfort her.”

Rocket snorts. “Comfort her? Have you met me?” He shakes his head. “What makes you
think she’d even want it to be me?”

Drax stares down at him pityingly, and suddenly, Rocket feels like the big guy thinks he is the
idiot.

It’s a weird realization. Absolutely frickin’ surreal.

“Spouses are meant to support each other,” the Kylosian explains patiently.
“What?!” It’s an undignified yelp but Rocket doesn’t have time to be embarrassed.
Everything in him balks at the Kylosian’s assumption. “I ain’t - we ain’t -“

“I may not understand the purpose of sarcasm, Rocket, but I am coming to recognize it,”
Drax interjects, sounding annoyed. “I do not appreciate you using it now.”

Rocket’s fur is bristling every which way and his skin feels inflamed and prickly with panic.
“Why the hell would you think this is sarcasm?!”

Drax sighs, long-suffering, and sounds like he’s quoting a textbook. “When someone says
something everyone knows to be untrue -“

“It’s not frickin’ untrue, you giant moron!” Rocket’s voice is something close to a strangled
scream. “I’m not - we ain’t spouses.”

Drax rolls his eyes, the gesture so exaggerated that his whole head moves. “Lovers, then.”

“What? Fu - No. No!”

Drax is just eyeing him dubiously, and Rocket bows his shoulders, drops his head, and
pinches the bridge of his narrow nose, trying to breathe through his exasperation.
Unbelievable.

“You are truly not married?” Drax asks at last, clearly still skeptical.

“No,” Rocket snaps. “We ain’t nothin’ like married. I don’t know why the - “ he cuts himself
because Groot is watching him with big, curious eyes, and he just knows a dropped fuck will
come back to haunt him. “I don’t know why the hell you’d think that.”

“Is she not the little one’s mother?”

“I am Groot!”

“Fu - goddammit. No. Groot, no. Drax, no. Everybody, no!”

“I am Groot,” the Flora Colossus pouts.

Drax’s eyes narrow like he’s not buying any of this. “Does she know you are not lovers?”

“I hate everything,” Rocket says to the ceiling.

“I am Groot!”

“I do not believe you,” Drax decides, overriding the need for Rocket to answer his previous
question. “But even if what you say is true, then you are clearly on the path of courtship, and
you should still go to her.”

“I can’t frickin’ believe this,” Rocket mutters, shaking his head.
There is a moment of silence and when Rocket looks down again, both Drax and little Groot
are watching him, waiting.

Fuck.

“Fine,” he snaps, and points a claw at Groot. “That means you gotta come to bed early too,”
he orders, and he can already see the mutinous jut of Groot’s tiny chin.

“I am Groot!”

“I can keep the little one tonight,” Drax offers reasonably. “Jolie is distraught. She may yell,
or cry. There is no reason for the child to see his mother in such a state before bed.”

“She is not his mother,” Rocket snaps. “And she wouldn’t yell.”

But he suddenly remembers her quiet face in the golden glow of the cockpit that night he’d
found her weeping, and the way she’d soundlessly swallowed her grief, trapping every
aching sob deep in her lungs, the same way he has.

Drax is right. Groot doesn’t need to see that.

“Besides,” Drax says reasonably, “sometimes the best way to offer comfort is through sexual
congress - “

“Shutthefuckuprightnow,” Rocket snarls, forgetting his own self-imposed restriction on
certain curses. He just needs the words to stop coming out of Drax’s mouth as quickly as
frickin’ possible.

Drax looks utterly nonplussed, but closes his mouth. For a minute, Rocket struggles to
organize his thoughts and grapple his indignation. Finally, he speaks.

“Fine. Groot can stay with you tonight.”

“I am Groot,” Groot replies reassuringly.

“Do not beat up Drax,” Rocket says tiredly, and begins collecting his own things - no leaving
weapons and explosives out, especially with a child, Gamora had said, and Jo had concurred.

Groot responds by scampering across the coffee table, launching himself onto Drax’s knee,
and pummeling the Kylosian in the flank. Rocket rolls his eyes, finishes gathering his things,
and cautiously retreats to their shared bunk.

The chamber is already dark.

On silent feet, he enters, sliding his belongings onto the workbench with a whisper. He’ll put
it away later. When he climbs onto the shelf-bed, Jo’s turned to face the wall. He hesitates,
then remembers how he’d recoiled from her touch earlier. The memory has him flinching in
the dark. Hesitantly, he reaches out a hand to comb his claws through her hair. It’s a little dull
right now and when he touches it, it’s still damp, like she’d towel-dried it after a shower.
Regret hits him hard and fast and sharp. He should’ve been down here sooner. Because
they’re copilots, and because she’s the best friend he’s got now, and because she’s patiently
stayed with him through all of his own stupid shit. And now she’s asleep, and he hasn’t had
time to -

To what? he thinks cynically. To sit with her in the dark while she cries? She’d been so good
at consoling him when Groot died, at just sharing space with him in a way that made room
for his grief and pain but didn’t abandon him to it. She’d helped him plant Groot and she’d
asked him for stories. She’d been so careful in easing his panicky breaths the night after
Knowhere and every nightmare since, and she’d been so willing to sleep on the floor that first
night he’d asked her to stay in Conjunction.

He can build a bomb from scratch in ten seconds or less, but he doesn’t know how to do any
of that.

After a reluctant moment, he just opts to delicately skate his clawed fingers through her hair
again, carefully untangling a damp, stray knot knitted into the end of one lock, and then curls
up under the covers, a wreath of fur and heat against her warm back.

“Sorry, princess,” he whispers into the dark shadows beneath the blankets.

He startles a little when she rolls toward him, carefully - not asleep after all, apparently. Her
hand finds his shoulder and back cautiously, like she’s giving him time to pull away again.
When he doesn’t move, she ruffles the fur gently.

“I’m sorry,” she whispers back, and he can feel her take a breath to say something more
before she hesitates, then sighs. “I just get some kind of way when we talk about… about
leaving people behind.” Even from under the covers, he can hear her swallow heavily. Her
hand rests on him, a light and comforting weight, and he uncurls so he can stick his head out
from under the blankets and peer at her in the dark. Eye-to-eye, she opens her mouth again,
closes it, then closes her eyes. She’s shaking her head. She tries again. Fails again.

He wants her to just tell him whatever’s going on, whatever he can do to make things better
for her right now. But there’s something about the expression on her face - the furrowed
brow, the aborted attempts to speak. It’s all too familiar.

He knows what it’s like for a person to have a story they can’t bring themselves to tell.

He hesitates and then, instead of saying anything at all, he reaches one hand out again. A
streamer of hair has fallen across her face; he plucks it up and tucks it back.

She lets out a kind of shuddering sigh and something in her relaxes. When he lets his fingers
skate over another strand, she leans in, and with his low-light vision, he sees her mouth
tremble.

That moron Drax was right.

Not that they were lovers - that’s too idiotic for words, no matter how tempting the fantasy
might be - but that Rocket should’ve been here from the beginning.
Rocket knows he’s a creature of impulse. He always has been, since long before he’d
engineered a spontaneous escape attempt from CounterEarth that had resulted only in tragedy
and pain. So maybe it shouldn’t surprise him so much that he’s reaching out, without any
conscious intention. One clawed hand cups the back of Jo’s head, lacing through the damp
hair, and tugs her forward to tuck her face under his chin. Her cheek is nestled just a hair’s
breadth from his throat, and she shudders again, melting under his hand and into the thin
mattress. Melting because of him.

“Thank you,” she whispers against him, and for some reason, the words hurt.

He swallows, and rests his chin on top of her hair, and waits until she falls asleep.

++++

He wakes up probably only a moment after Jo does. It’s as if, even at rest, he can feel the
anxiety hit her as soon as she regains consciousness. Her wakefulness pulls him awake too,
and he finds himself petting the back of her head before he’s even fully alert, because
apparently neither of them have moved all night.

He doesn’t know when he became so attuned to her.

“You good?” he rasps, his voice hoarse from disuse and sleep. He’s still stroking the crown of
her head, and her hair has dried into silk at some point in the night. The strands slip over his
fingers.

“Can we stay here just a second longer?” she whispers, and something in him cracks open
because she sounds like she’s dreading whatever’s outside the bunk door, and he’s never
heard her sound like that before.

As long as you want, he thinks, but doesn’t say. He just keeps petting.

She’s true to her word though - it’s only a moment more before she stirs, letting him
disentangle his claws from her hair. She looks at him with shadows under her eyes and if he
didn’t know better, he’d think she hadn’t slept at all. She shifts toward him, a fleetingly quick
movement, and for a moment he thinks she’s going to drop an impulsive kiss on the top of his
head, the way she does to Groot and Quill.

At the last second, she shies away, and he’s stunned by his own unexpected disappointment.

By the time they make their way up through the hatch, the others are already gathered in the
common room. No-one’s made breakfast - looks like we’re all punishing ourselves with plain
black coffee this morning, Rocket notices grimly.

Jo’s already moving toward Drax, letting Groot jump from the Kylosian’s shoulder to hers.
The little Flora Colossus catches himself with a streamer of her hair, but she doesn’t even
wince, murmuring some sweet good morning words while the little guy nuzzles into her
cheek.
“I think we just can’t worry about it,” Gamora’s saying from the sofa, but her voice is heavy
with dread. “There are plenty of other, more worthwhile jobs we could be doing. My sister
doesn’t need saving, and she wouldn’t want it, to be honest.” Gamora looks away. “Not from
me.”

Quill looks exhausted, and Drax is staring stoically into the middle-distance, arms crossed.

“Lookin’ cheerful,” Rocket observes. “We makin’ the big decisions this morning, then?”

Jo smiles, but it’s already pale and worried. Her bottom lip is swollen, like she’s been
chewing it all night. Maybe she had been - he hadn’t been in a position to see her face for
most of it, after all. He suddenly bets, if he could see her hands, that the base of her nails
would be bloodied and torn like they’d been when he’d gotten out of the Kyln.

Worse still, her eyes are flicking between him and Gamora nervously, and she seems…
spooked. She opens her mouth like she’s gonna say something - then closes it. It’s last night
all over again.

“Gamora,” Quill says instead. “We’re here for you. Everybody’s family is…is hard. Messed
up. We can do whatever you want. If there’s any part of you that wants to try and get her…
you know, we can turn her in for the bounty, if you want. Drop her off with the Nova Corps
and let her do her time in the Kyln. Or…”

“Or what?” Gamora asks, her voice suddenly sharp. “Really, what? Keep her on the Gemma
Lynn and rehabilitate her?”

“I don’t - I don’t know,” Quill scrambles. “Something. If we pick her up - if we have her -
you’ll have time to think about it. We can come up with something.”

Gamora is shaking her head. “It’s over. I’ve tried. So many times. She doesn’t want - she
doesn’t want anything to do with me. The fact that I’m trying to do something good here -
with all of you - is only going to drive her further away. It’s only going to make her want to
be…worse. Or whatever.” She sucks in a breath. “The Sovereign won’t execute her. The
bounty is too good. Someone else will pick her up.”

Rocket bites his tongue against the urge to point out that if the bounty’s that good, they might
as well do the job anyway. He suspects that his perspective will not be appreciated right now.
Instead, he weaves between them and takes a seat at the bar while Jo pours them both cups of
coffee. The coffee smells acrid - someone must’ve let it set and burn.

And he’d been right. The first two fingers on both of her hands are shredded.

“And then what?” Jo says, the first words out of her mouth. She’s staring at the rim of
Rocket’s coffee cup as she slides it to him, like it’s an anchor. “What happens then?”

Gamora spreads her open palms and fingers. Who knows? she’s saying, or maybe: it will be
out of my hands.
“Do you want to try? To get her back? To really get her back?” Jo asks. Her voice is achingly
soft. “It’s okay to say no, but you need to answer the question, one way or the other.”

Everyone else goes quiet.

“Take out the whole idea of the bounty,” Jo says, like that’s the most reasonable thing to do -
and in Jo’s weird mind, it probably does seem reasonable - “or what you think you should do,
what you think is a better use of time.” She pauses. Swallows. “Is there anything in you that
wants her to be your sister again, if you have the chance?”

The former assassin starts to say something, but her voice cracks, and she smothers it.
Gamora looks completely at a loss and for a moment, Rocket recognizes an echo of it in
himself. For a second, that spot behind his sternum cracks open again, a little bit of
heartbreak shared with the Zen-Whoberian.

He rubs his knuckles against the center of his chest, hard, and forces it closed.

Then Jo’s gently depositing Groot on the counter next to him. She glides out of the
kitchenette, around the bar, and drops to a crouch in front of Gamora. Rocket’s brain
suddenly pulls up the booze-blurred memory of her kneeling on the hexagonal pavers of
Conjunction, her shins and kneecaps pressed into the booze and the glass, and he’s abruptly
filled with so much regret that he can taste it.

I came looking for you. I was worried. Do you want to come home?

A better person would’ve gone down to the bunk the moment that she did last night. A better
friend would’ve not needed to be talked into acting like he cared by frickin’ Drax of all
people.

Jo’s reaching out. She takes both of Gamora’s slender, deadly hands in hers.

“Listen to me,” Jo says, and even though that gentleness isn’t directed at him right now, it
still cracks open that spot in his chest even further. Gamora looks up from her lap and their
joined hands, and sees something in Jo’s eyes that holds her.

“If there’s any part of you that will wonder what could have been, then you cannot walk
away from your sister right now.”

Quill makes a noise in this throat unexpectedly, and probably unintentionally: a soft,
sympathetic little sound. Rocket doesn’t spare him a glance, though. Something is happening
here. Something is rising close to the surface. His eyes are locked on Jo, and his fists clench
so tightly that he can feel his own claws prick and draw blood from his palms.

“I know your relationship with Nebula is … complicated.” The Terran girl takes a deep,
shaky breath. She holds the Zen-Whoberian’s gaze. “But I also know what it’s like to leave a
sister behind, and then to lose her.”

Something drops in Rocket’s chest. The gaping maw behind his sternum becomes a black
hole, a vacuum.
  Jolie chews her lip, then looks away, and shakes her head - hard.

  “I promise you. You will spend every breath for the rest of your life wondering if you could
  have done something, anything, to make things turn out differently.”

  Gamora twists her hands in Jo’s gentle grasp, wringing them. Her whisper is wrenching. “My
  sister and I are already beyond that possibility.”

  But Jo’s already shaking her head again. She squeezes the assassin’s fingers.

  “As long as she’s still alive, anything’s possible.” Her words wobble. “Don’t wait. Not one
  fucking second, Gamora.”

   Quill sends a transmission to Sovereign, and figures they have a cycle and a half to get there
   in time for the abilisk migration. They’ll need to fly steadily, but at an easy pace. Groot has
   crossed the counter to throw himself on Drax and climb over the big Kylosiasn. “I am
   Groot,” he says, pointing to Gamora, and Drax sets the small Flora Colossus on the couch
   beside the miserable Zen-Whoberian. The little guy tugs on Gamora’s sleeve until she picks
   him up and lets him cuddle into her shoulder.

   Jo immediately tucks herself away in the cockpit.

   “My turn to fly,” she says over her shoulder lightly as she goes, like she hasn’t just set off a
   gravity bomb in Rocket’s chest. He can’t shake the memory of her kneeling in the glass and
   the booze, gently pushing aside his laser cannon and looking up at him with those big,
   luminous eyes.

   I came looking for you. I was worried.

   Do you want to come home?

   Let’s go together.

   And then carrying him all the way to the Gemma Lynn on her frickin’ back with his teeth

   He turns on a clawed foot to follow her.

   For a second, Rocket considers ignoring Quill entirely. It’s bad frickin’ timing. Rocket has a

   But for whatever reason - maybe his own cowardice still coming up to bite his heels, because

“Yeah, Star-Boy?”

Quill rolls his eyes right back. “All right, Ranger Rick. Can I talk to you?”

Rocket’s ears flatten. “Right now?” He imagines Jo’s already folded herself into the pilot’s
chair and set coordinates. Sure enough, he hears the faint hum of the flight engines coming to
life, buzzing softly through the floor beneath his feet.

Quill just gestures him closer, ducking into the airlock bay, a little removed from the common
area where the other three are currently quietly sitting. Rocket follows, rounding the bend
into the small space with caution. He’s not sure what this is about, but Quill’s never asked to
talk to him one-on-one, so he hazards a guess that it can’t be good.

When he looks up, Quill’s waiting, hands on hips and an inscrutable expression in his face.

“Yeah, I guess I was right. You look like a raccoon who’s definitely just heard something he
didn’t wanna hear.”

Rocket can feel his fur bristle, skin prickling with something like static. “Don’t call me that,”
he growls.

Quill tsks. “You were with her last night?”

Rocket stares back, giving this jackass his most dead-eyed expression. “We do sleep
together.”

Okay, maybe not the most innocent choice of words, but it’s good to see Quill flinch a little.
Doesn’t stop the nosy Terran from prying, though.

“So. How did that go?”

He rolls his eyes. “Classy, Star-Dork. I don’t know about Terrans, but I personally think it’s

Quill clucks his tongue in irritation. “You’re such an asshole,” the humie mutters under his

“I know you seem really concerned with where I’m putting my dick.”

“Dammit, you little - this isn’t about - that. I’m just trying to ask if you wanna talk about…
what Jolie said in there.”

Something quizzical and nervous flickers up inside Rocket’s aching chest cavity. He stomps
the unfamiliar sensation as soon as he feels it. “What’s there to talk about?”

“Oh, I dunno,” Quill says sarcastically. “The fact that the girl you love just told a roomful of
people about the most miserable moments of her life. The cliffnotes version, but still.”

The girl you love? Rocket’s fur nearly stands on end and his ears fully flatten again, as if he
were already under attack. Drax must be running his idiot mouth.
Rocket plans to sneer, to make a mockery of Quill’s statement. A hundred cutting words rise
in his mouth, most of them at Jo’s expense - and therefore, most of them things he’ll regret
later, probably enough to make himself sick with self-loathing. But he’s as surprised as
anyone when those aren’t the words that come out of his mouth.

“I don’t have any questions, an’ if I did, I’d ask her,” he snaps instead. “Can I go now?”

Quill’s eyes narrow on him. “Not yet.”

Rocket rolls his eyes. “Remind me why I kept you and the other idiots around after Xandar?”

Quill breathes a long-suffering sigh. “Because some part of that little raccoon brain of yours
knows we’re good for you.”

The words ring true, and Rocket hates it. He grits his teeth instead. “I told you to stop calling
me that.” He glowers up at the Terran. “You’re not exactly makin’ a strong case for yourself
here, Quill.”

“Rocket,” Quill says, his voice uncharacteristically quiet. “Hasn’t hanging out with Jo taught
you anything? You don’t gotta do everything alone.”

Everything in Rocket seizes up. “Fuck you, Quill.”

“I mean it, Rocket. I was with Jolie when she found out, okay? About her sister. And now,
with Gamora …” Quill shakes his head. “I’m just saying - I know what it’s like when there’s
